reviews.review:
Clocktower is located on the second floor, right above a bar. It was surprising that they were not booked out for a friday night. The decor was nice, it was dark but kinda of fit in with the whole vibe. We were seated right away and service was great. Only complaint was that I waited a really long time for my first cocktail. 

The complimentary bread and butter was pretty nice. We started with the tuna tartare, the spicy mayo was very unique in terms that I have never had this combination at other places. But my boyfriend and I both agreed that we had wish there were some sort of cracker or chips with it. 

The seared scallops were perfectly done, the grapes added a little sweet ting to the whole dish. And the cauliflower puree was exceptional. We ended with the beef wellington and I had to say was a great way to end the night. The mashed potatoes was really good. The greens were cut in different proportions which was kind of annoying. The wellington itself was kinda salty but because it was good overall I didn't take any points off.

Probably the worse dining experience at NYC. As a foodie who been eating fancy restaurants around the whole manhattan for 6 years. Never seen anything that bad. Told me they have a table at 7 pm. Arrived at 7 and they said have to wait til 8. Hours of waiting and still no table. Don't come.

reviews.review:
Came here for restaurant week and was generally underwhelmed. 

I was in the party with Lauren M., and as she mentioned, we weren't seated until 7:45 for a 7:30 reservation. We also had to ask for the restaurant week menus, which is off-putting as it feels like they don't want to offer it to you. 

The usual menu is on the smaller side, so I ordered off the restaurant week menu. The beer selection was minimal and they were actually out of 1-2 cocktails, so that menu was limited as well. 

Everything seemed to take forever. The wait staff was attentive but the appetizers and entrees were slow to come out. 

Overall the food wasn't anything special, it was generally bland and better options are available at the high end price point.

This place is ok in terms of decor and location. The food is average and the service leaves room for improvement. 

We had a reservation for 7:30PM and we arrived promptly. We were not seated until 7:45PM. 

The restaurant itself is pretty small, one room for the dining tables and another room for the bar, plus a small room with a pool table.

They are having restaurant week but did not give us the restaurant week menu so I had to ask for it.

I'm a vegetarian and the vegetarian options are limited in entrees down to a pasta dish or a risotto dish featured for restaurant week.

I didn't see any vegan options.

The cocktail menu is small but I ordered a Ritual. It was good.

I opted not to do the restaurant week menu because I didn't want risotto. I had the agnolotti from the regular menu which was pretty good.

The other members in my party were lukewarm on the food. Two members ordered steak cooked different ways but when their steaks come out, they were cooked pretty much the same.

They give you free bread to start and that was actually very good with salt butter. If you wanted more, there was a $5 up charge.

We each had dessert. I had a salted caramel custard bar, everyone else had the restaurant week desserts including the ice cream and the panna cotta. I think we all enjoyed the dessert but it was not anything groundbreaking.

They have an abundance of waitstaff and they cleared plates pretty quickly, even before we were done with them for the bread. We had to ask the server to bring us new plates for the second bread course.

There are two bathrooms located in the restaurant. The space is accessible by elevator. You have to enter on the 24th Street side and use the elevator bank to go to the restaurant.

The door staff on the ground floor of the hotel were very nice. The hotel bar in the lobby seems nice too.

The food is not cheap but the value and quality is just not there. You can have better food for the same price in other restaurants in midtown.

Each course took a while to come out too. We were there over two hours with most of it spent waiting on food.

Overall a pretty average experience. I don't think I'd come back for dinner, but I'd consider coming to the bar for a drink. The bar area doesn't have many seats other than a few at the bar itself.

Disclaimer: if I was judging just the complimentary bread and butter, it would be 5/5. We had like 3 loaves of that with the salted butter, and it is one of the best bread and butter I've had ever.

However, the beef Wellington was a bit of a let-down. The beef in the Wellington was of good quality. However, I wish the mushroom duxelles were a bit more flavourful and the pastry felt undercooked and overly thick. The fish in the tomato broth was quite good, the broth was creamy and tangy.

I was not a huge fan of the desserts, in particular the sticky toffee pudding. The sticky toffee pudding was a hard sticky, like biting into caramel. I was expecting and would much prefer the moist toffee cake. The flavors of the desserts were good and very creative, and the presentation was great however.

The service was super good and attentive especially with my obscene bread and butter requests. And the ambiance was super classy, especially with the beautiful staircase.

Overall, for the pretty hefty price, I would not come back (well maybe I would just for the bread and butter).
Loved this hotel bar (and I wasn't even staying here). Really cute decor and the drinks are delicious. The staff was super attentive and there were plenty of open seats on a Saturday night.

We visited on a Friday night with a last-minute booking. We arrived early and grabbed a drink at the bar before being seated. There's also a pool area, which adds a nice, friendly touch to the venue. I found out they used to have a Michelin star but lost it in 2022--makes me wonder why. The restaurant is located on the second floor, though I had expected it to be inside the clocktower itself!

We were welcomed with some bread and butter to start. For our meal, we ordered the tuna tartare, fish and chips, beef Wellington for 2, and panna cotta for dessert. The beef Wellington was definitely the highlight--perfectly cooked and full of flavor. However, we felt the plating of the tuna tartare could have been better. The panna cotta was a great way to end the meal, with the raspberry sorbet adding a refreshing tartness to balance the sweetness.

The service was on the slower side, but I got the sense they wanted us to relax and take our time, so it worked out fine for a leisurely evening.

Ambiance is impeccable. The cool design, color palette, photographs, pool table are all aspirational on so many levels. 
When we came it was quiet since it was towards the end of brunch. But it was just right - we had a great conversation and shared good food. 
Scottish egg..recommend! 
Fish and chips..proper and good!
We wanted a mid day bite and that's what we got. The sauce for the fish and chips was unexpected..it was a sort of Indian fusion. 
The servers were prompt, nothing good or bad to say other than we got our food in a good time frame. 
I loved dining here. I'd definitely come back to try more dishes. And I'd imagine dinner here is stellar too.

Visited initially for the restaurant week experience. But to our surprise, we were not offered the restaurant week menu until requested. Moreover, none of the recommended/signature dish is in the restaurant week menu. So we decided to go with the regular menu.

Overall, the taste is basically align with expectation and all dishes are a little bit salty to me. 

Scallop is tender and I like the combination with yellow beets and cauliflowers. 

Beef Wellington is what we came for. It's quite large portion (I eventually only ate half of it). The flavors are good and again just slightly salty to me (especially the mushroom)

Shishito pepper - a side dish; quite satisfied with the portion given the price. We were informed there is no asparagus today and shishito pepper is a substitute. This pepper doesn't have any spicy taste but has the freshness. A good buddy to the beef. Plus, this is the only one I don't think it's salty.

Dessert is Toffle pudding - a bit too sweet to me; quite pretty in look (remember to have your phone ready earlier if you would like to take a pic or video when the toffle is poured)

Wow! We had such a terrific experience here! If you make it there before your reservation, there is a bar when you walk in, one upstairs too and a pool table upstairs.  

The staircase is so pretty. The dining area too is so beautiful and takes you back in time. Their service was impeccable! They were on point and so friendly. We loved our waiter! 

Now, let's talk about their food! 
Everything we ordered was delicious! The portions were decently sized and I really like how they spaced out each course. We weren't rushed and we were able to enjoy each selection without feeling stuffed. 

I really like how they showed us the beef Wellington before it was cooked and I also enjoyed watching their Baked Alaska presentation. 

Everything was absolutely perfect from start to finish! We also had time to play a game of pool!
The English breakfast was excellent.  Sausage was my favorite.  Baked bean and American bacon was great.  Nice ambiance and service. Highly recommend.
the food was great and excellent service overall! i would definitely come back again! the only thing confusing was how to navigate to the restaurant through the elevators.

So good! Beautiful space, delicious food and drinks, and good service. 

They do a phenomenal job balancing cozy with modern, which isn't easy.

The duck and scallops were both delicious. And the staff go out of their way to make sure you feel taken care of.

The place is gorgeous, great vibe

The service was INCREDIBLE. When the hostess asked if we were celebrating something, I mentioned it was my wife's birthday, genuinely not expecting anything, but at least three people in the staff came over to say happy birthday and they even left a cute note on the table before we sat down, really top notch

The food was great, in particular the burger and the Scottish egg

We're certainly coming back

This is a hidden gem! It's located on the second floor of the Edition Hotel. When standing in the park, look for the building with the clock and you'll spot it right away. lol. Three of us went for brunch and we all enjoyed our meals... crab cakes and avocado toast, and bloody Marys. Service was friendly and well paced. Afterwards we moved to the bar and enjoyed some cocktails. The greenpoint and marayuca were awesome. I could've had 10 of them but I didn't. The space is bit dark but fun and there's a room with a pool table. I recommend popping in for food or drinks or both.

Yesterday, we celebrated my boyfriend's birthday at the restaurant, and while the food was good, our experience was overshadowed by the demeanor of our server, Eduardo, who made us feel uncomfortable by acting as though he was above us. 

A few examples would include: almost throwing the complimentary birthday dessert on the table as well as the check even we did not ask for it, we also asked him to pause on lighting the candle because we wanted to take a video but he ignored our wishes and lit it up anyways. Both my friend and I were sure to ask this vocally multiple times so he definitely heard us. We also advised him early on that I was allergic to almonds so anything with nuts I wanted to be extra careful, the complimentary birthday dessert had nuts and nothing was told to me until I bit into it already. The attention to detail lacked greatly and the human touch is not there which degrades the entire atmosphere of the restaurant. 

We will go back to the clocktower again because the food itself is good but Eduardo left a such an impression that I will ask that my server is NOT him when I return. I hope the management team will take steps to properly train their staff in customer service as this is crucial to any restaurant business. 

You can't have great food for with shitty service.. deducted 3 stars because of service.

Came here for a dinner with a friend and really enjoyed the ambiance. The beef wellington was to die for. The meat was very tender and the pastry was buttery and flakey. We also enjoyed the beef carpaccio. Service was a bit slow but the food was worth the wait.
Very romantic and sexy vibe. Great find on restaurant week. The pool table was a pleasant surprise and an added bonus. Will definitely return

A cozy environment with an oak themed feel to it.  The food was very good.  Highly recommend the butternut squash soup.  The duck was amazing, cooked according to preference with a nice crusty shell.  Fish and chips were the Americanized edition.  Good but not authenticate British tasting fish batter.  And then the sticky toffee dessert was 100% authentic.  The staff were attentive and quite prompt with the food.
I recommend this restaurant and likely will be back.

We ate dinner at the Clock Tower for Restaurant Week.  We were not presented with the restaurant week menu when we sat down and had to ask for it.  We noticed other tables having to do the same.  However, the menus did arrive with a recommendation for the most expensive item on the menu (Beef Wellington, $71).  

We ordered a dozen oysters and then the three course Restaurant Week special for each of us. The oysters were fresh and tasty.  However, they were brought to the table with the appetizers, which was odd.  The appetizers (steak tartare and a salad) were OK, but a little small. The entree was a hanger steak with potatoes.  A photo is included.  It had to be the worst presented plate I've ever had at a NYC restaurant.  Worse yet, the (medium rare) steak was over salted and tough.  The potatoes were flavorful, but lukewarm.  The deserts were just OK.  The panna cotta was topped with a citrus salad, a weird flavor combination that did not work.  

Besides the issue with the menus, the service was problematic. We sat for a long time before being initially greeted and long time periods passed between courses.  The numerous waitstaff were all young and inexperienced.

In photos, the restaurant looked romantic.  In reality, it was very noisy. The tables for two are very narrow and long, forcing you to sit far apart.  That, combined with the noise, made it impossible to carry on a conversation at a normal volume. Most of the noise was the loud music from the nearby bar.  

Overall, the visit was a disappointment. Restaurant week is a great time to try new places.  Sadly, we learned that we did not like the Clock Tower and that we will not be back.

Also, despite what other reviews claim, the Clock Tower is not a one-Michelin starred restaurant.  The list is here: https://guide.michelin.com/us/en/new-york-state/new-york/restaurants/1-star-michelin?sort=distance.  Its not even close to the standard set by those establishments.

Great spot, inside the Edition hotel. Seafood platter is a must try. Delicious. Highly enjoyed the halibut. Everyone had great meals. Drink was good (not great). Good service (attentive waiter who gave good suggestions). I would definitely go back.

Came here for a friend's birthday - excellent food and service here, highly recommended if you like british cuisine or just want beef wellington. The only thing that takes a star away is their portions are kind of small, but amazing otherwise!

The Clocktower Restaurant is in what must be one of the finest hotel properties in Manhattan - the New York Edition. The restaurant feels like an exclusive old school club that is equal parts hip, chic and timelessly stylish. The gallery walls are gorgeous and the intentionally-curated photo collection is interesting in and of itself. The food is a sure thing. I've dined there 4 times. Three of those times it felt like a Michelin-starred experience - every "chip" (French fry) was crispy perfection, fresh smoothies, no detail of our meal left unattended and impeccable service. 
Last weekend was a miss, however. The restaurant was not crowded yet our waiter took our order and we never saw him again except to either bring the check or remove our plates. A kitchen hand served us and we had to flag him down while he served a nearby table to request our check. The waiter brought it to us but without asking if we wanted anything else; we felt rushed at that point. We would have had another round of drinks or dessert but for lack of service. It was a very nice meal but I was disappointed that the experience didn't rise to the level I have seen on previous visits. 
The Clocktower is so special! I hope we were there on a rare "off" Saturday when its best talent was taking holiday time off.

Dived in for the number one listed English Breakfast in NYC. It was very good, eggs needed slightly longer, sausages were excellent, beans, tomato and mushroom were fine. I wanted the toast for fried bread but sadly they didnt know what that was (bread crisp fried in the bacon fat). Struggled a bite to get Tea but likely my English accent. Overall very good but i have a few more to try before i declare it the best. 

Service was great.

Ambiance refined.

Was at a private party in the Clocktower bar restaurant tonight ... the girls and guy working as hosts and party entrance were about as rude and distasteful as there is.  

Talk about a buzz kill and bad energy ... not a place to have fun or a party.

The Clocktower offers a taste of modern London in the heart of bustling NYC. 

This One Michelin Star restaurant specializes in elevated and contemporary British cuisine. With three cozy dining rooms, a dedicated billiards room, and a vibrant bar, it provides a multifaceted dining experience.

I really hate to do this, but I must downgrade The Clocktower from 5 to 3 stars. I can see why they lost their Michelin star. Let me explain: if we had never been here before, we would have been perfectly happy with our experience on Saturday night. However, if you read my previous review you'll see that our visit in 2021 was virtually perfect. Let me get into what has changed:
1. The service. It was not bad. Not at all but this time around it lacked polish and was a little clumsy. All the servers were friendly and competent but the last time we felt like were being pampered by an entire brigade of top notch service that ran like a well oiled machine. One runner was polite and super friendly but at one point he came over to swipe the crumbs off our table and he elbowed my water glass. Also, he had long hair and he had two long bits of hair  hanging off the front of his face that kind if brushed on my shoulder and near my face. This same service knocked very hard into my husband's shoulder. It could happen to anyone but it points to the lack of training and polish that was present at our last visit. 

2. The food. It was meh. I had the Scotch egg and it was much smaller than expected because it turned out to be a quail egg. It tasted fine but the walnut ketchup was delicious. My husband has the butternut squash soup and that was excellent. It was complex with a nice balance of sweet and savory. For his entree he chose the beef Wellington. The portion exceptionally small given its price: $64. We were expecting an individual Wellington and he got a modest slice from a larger piece. For the price, it really should have been two. Although he said the dish was delicious. He just wished he had more. I tried the potatoes that came as a side and they were excellent. I ordered the fish and chips expecting a more elevated dish than what you would expect at a pub. It was fine. The batter on the fish was nothing special but the fish itself was fresh and well cooked.  The triple cooked chips were something you would expect at a family chain restaurant. The tartar sauce was very good. For dessert my husband had the bruleed nutmeg cheesecake. I didn't try it but he said it was good, but once again, very small portion for $18. I had the baked Alaska and I didn't realize it was for two and it was huge. But the apple flavors were very good and they flambed it at the table which was a nice touch. 
All in all, we left very disappointed because it had slipped so far from our previous experience. I know it's highly rated but I think if people had known it in its prior form, maybe they would not rate it so high. So sad. I'll hold on to the memories of our first visit.

The restaurant is beautiful but... what kind of server would sarcastically say "Who brings food to a restaurant?" to a bday girl with cake on her hand?!! Was very happy entering the restaurant but suddenly got ruined.

INy. Just so you know. 
The Clock Tower is very fancy and very pricey. The kind of place where the staff is just a little bit better than you. We had a great time and a very NYC experience. 
We arrived early and No, we could not wait at the bar for our friend, but we're seated at our table. No reason why, just "no, I can't seat you at the bar".
My husband, a native Californian, who is used to chatting up the server, hemmed and hawed over what wine he wanted to drink and the server lost interest and walked away. Remember when the job was called "waiter" ? This happened 3 times during our meal, which I thought was hilarious. The server was not really rude, just not interested in waiting.
The Beef Wellington was out of this world, could not be better. I love duck and this was outstanding and the largest portion of duck I have had, in a restaurant.
Though England is not know for fine cuisine, this was off the charts delicious from start to finish. The ambience is quiet, relaxed and upscaled library that serves food.
I totally reccomend this for a special occasion meal or if you just have leftover money in your budget.

Fantastic vibe ! Went there for dinner and location and building were amazing. 
Food was also great can't complain. 
Tuna tar tar is always amazing , steak was pure, lobster was so good! That sauce that juice is amazing. 
Soufflé was amazing. Im telling you to get this desert if you are here.  And peppermint tea to end ! 
Went in for birthday left very satisfied. 
Service is top notch as well.

Service was exceptional, food was great, the ambiance was charming and elegant. Would definitely go back. The price per portion was as you'd expect from a restaurant of this caliber. Cocktails were tasty and we were gifted with some chocolates at the end of our meal for my birthday. Overall 9.7/10

We reserved 2 seats tonight with the Clocktower for our wedding anniversary. The major selling point for us was definitely seeing beef wellington on the menu, as we had been looking for a good reference for the amazing dish on Masterchef. I am glad to say that our experience (along with the wellington) did not disappoint in the slightest!

Despite coming early, our hostess was very accomodating and found us seats. The room was dimly lit and it definitely contributed to a more intimate feeling despite the other people around us. We were greeted with a beautiful handwritten card congratulating us on our anniversary. Another thing that made us feel more cozy was the glasses of champagne they set us up with!

We ordered 2 scotch eggs and 2 beef wellingtons. The complimentary bread and butter came out with the bread super warm and soft, and the butter saltier than   we were used to, but we still pleasantly enjoyed. The scotch eggs came with a mild walnut ketchup and salt and were tasty but I think that we will try one of the many other appetizing starters the next time we return.

Finally, the beef wellingtons were perfect. The meat was cooked perfect medium rare, the duxelle was so rich and flavorful, and the puff pastry was crispy. However, the real star for us was the amazing bone marrow gravy. It was to die for, and the extra gravy we got went on everything- mash, carrots, and wellington- on the plate. We will definitely be returning for this dish!

Thank you to the amazing staff at the Clocktower for an amazing anniversary that we will not forget!

Went here for our wedding anniversary. What can I say, this place was almost perfect. We got our reservations mixed up and arrived a whole hour early. The hostess was so nice and found a way to squeeze us in. All staff was very friendly and on top of our needs. The beef Wellington was magical. That sauce they used as gravy for the mash was out of this world. The carrots were a bit undercooked but everything else made up for it. We were even given free wine and a cute little hand written card as a congratulations for our anniversary. I would definitely come here again just for this one dish and the service.

Incredible experience! Worth every penny! From the moment we got there until we left, the service was outstanding. We felt so welcomed and pampered. They generously gave us a complimentary glass of champagne since we were celebrating our anniversary! The beef Wellington was out of this world; we ordered it medium and it came out cooked perfectly. The poached halibut was also delicious! The bread was also phenomenal! I'd highly recommend this spot for a special occasion! I can't wait to come back!

It has been a while since I've been to a restaurant that truly blew me away. Let me start with the service. I made reservations through Resy and noted I was celebrating an anniversary. The host immediately said congratulations. He was smiling the entire time and made us feel welcomed. We were seated right away without any wait.

Our server greeted us and provided us complimentary champagne for our anniversary. We were given a wine menu and asked if we wanted to speak with the sommelier.

We ordered the beef wellington and poached halibut. The beef was cooked perfectly medium (the way we ordered it) and the bone marrow gravy was delicious. The halibut was tender and the lemon butter sauce had the perfect amount of seasoning.

We finished the meal with their sticky toffee cake.

Overall it was an expensive dinner but for a special occasion it was perfect. If you can request Ivan as your server. He was very attentive and added to the dining experience.

A wonderful dining experience with superb service and food. The seared scallops were nicely seared and had great flavor. We enjoyed the tasty crab cocktail tart and the roasted beetroot salad. 

The beef Wellington was beautifully cooked and paired nicely with the bone marrow gravy. The poached halibut with lemon butter sauce was cooked perfectly. One of my favorite dishes of the night was the cavateli pasta with blue crab and asparagus. The lemon pasta sauce was divine and refreshing. 

They have nice dessert options as well! The service was top notch and the manager was great. O
I'm looking forward to revisiting for another great dining experience.

Have heard great things about this restaurant for years and was excited to finally check it out. We started with the house bread and the shrimp cocktail. We then had the wedge salad, the Mac and cheese (amazing) and then the tandoori chicken and the duck. Everything was amazing. For my drink I had pappys on the rocks. It was my first time having it and it was amazing. The service was great and the ambiance felt very old school. Great spot

The service and food were amazing. Everything was on-point from the moment we arrived to when we left. The beef Wellington and salmon stake were perfect. The only suggest I have is to turn down the music a tad as I couldn't hear half of what my wife was saying. Otherwise, the ambiance and decor were great as well. The bread served at the beginning of the meal was so flavorful and delicious.

So great spot cheap drinks and all that I normally have a great time here with friends but today Monday night this bald headed bar tender kicked us out cause a friends ID was expired when we come often and my iD was good. I just found it really weird if We all over 21 why kick us out cause one person ID is expired and we have all entered before ?? Like  . Fuck that bald headed bar tender
Literally amazing place great ambience delicious food, especially the chicken. The service was out of this world as well!

Love it when my "celery like soup" is actually poured table side instead of sloshed through a busy dining room. Honestly have no idea how some people are allowed to review fine dining experiences. I remember coming here when it originally opened. Can't wait to go back. I'm having a craving for Beef Wellington and it was divine here. Service impeccable.

Service, food were excellent.  Sound level was deafening in the room we ate in.  Upon my return from the rest room post dinner; walked into the other dining room..much quieter.  
Will NEVER go back as the sound level was unbearable 
alan

Breakfast edition : I haven't eaten here since they opened. This is one of the most sumptuous rooms in Manhattan in the Editor hotel. It's beyond English drawing room lux.
Ate and drank:
Egg white omelette plus ratatouille $21
Pain au chocolat $5
Currant scone $4
Drip coffee $5
Just eating here feels special and it is.
I love ratatouille and salad with my egg whites and this was a splashy treat. Skip the croissants and get the scone it's incredible! This is a Stephen Starr production & one of the best breakfast experiences albeit pricey in Manhattan.

Came for dinner. Beautifully decorated restaurant with fantastic staff and service on the second floor.

They brought out a small round loaf of bread and salted butter that was superb. We ordered the beef wellington and parsnip risotto. The beef wellington was divine (definitely pour all of the bone marrow gravy sauce they provide on top). It was cooked perfectly and the carrots and mashed potatoes were great sides to pair with it. It is quite expensive but at least you will enjoy it.

The risotto was good but was lacking in overall flavor. It was mostly just creamy and dense with an odd walnut and piece of parsnip. I am not sure I would order it again, but it was pleasant enough.

The atmosphere was beautiful but I was slightly disappointed by the service and food. We made a reservation for breakfast and as we were being seated they told us the kitchen was closing in 5 mins and that we had to order immediately.... Wish they told us that when we called to make the reservation.

The food was just okay. No one in our party thought it was anything special... not sure if the quality was lower because the kitchen was about to close? I expected a better experience due to the prestige the restaurant has.

This is part of the Starr restaurant group.  We had the opportunity to eat at another establishment this week.  It was supposedly rated higher than Clocktower.  The food there was subpar, the food and service at CT, absolutely exquisite and innovative.  The staff was completely attentive and friendly, like a family.  I can't wait to go back.

(Dined 12/10/2022 SA @ 6:30pm): I looked everywhere and couldn't recall a clock in this "tower" restaurant in New York's Flatiron District!

The Clocktower was the choice for my dear friend to celebrate her milestone 40th birthday with a party of four. Drawn by the interior photos and an Old World classic sensibility, would happy memories be made before the clock struck midnight!?

PURCHASE
Bread (Comp.): This freshly-baked round mound was so nice we had it twice https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=wlunf_qg3yrfsUsTVQ3yDQ&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw!

God Save The Quince Cocktail ($19.00): Made with Kettle One Vodka, blanc vermouth, spiced quince, and lemon juice, this was a vibrant sweet elixir with a twist of tartness that went down smoothly https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=DXuu8t0R2TLBE_DGnAaB7g&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

2021 Domaine De La Foret Gasselin Sancerre Loire Sauvignon Blanc 750ml Bottle ($88.00): A real cork, light yellow color, slight oak sweet aroma, low body, oak sweet tropical flavor, crisp finish, oak sweet aftertaste, and low astringency https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=SwL3q9Jx_1e75QdlsDvKqg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

Shellfish Platter ($65.00): A seafood spread of  1/2 Maine lobster, 6 medium-sized shrimp, and 6 oysters along with melted butter and other accoutrements, this was a nice starter sampler with everything chilled and fresh https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=ekj_yKjPkyGZhrYRLP8_Dw&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

Crispy Brussels Sprouts In Bacon Maple Vin ($12.00): This was a fragrant but somewhat cluttered side dish. However, it still tasted wonderful with a slight tartness from the vinaigrette https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=TI4Qv-uWqDKaYtzOZgICHQ&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

Macaroni & Cheese w/Wild Mushrooms and Slow-Cooked Ox Cheek ($19.00): This was far too fancy and not what I expected. More of a sample pasta dish, I liked the flavors but failed on portion, presentation, and price https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=nrFIfNV0msK30W83Kd3FXQ&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

Berkshire Pork Chop w/Bubble and Squeak Cake, Apple and Fennel Salad ($34.00): A small but meaty tender portion, I could've done with less plating and more portion because I felt the effects were minimal and didn't add much to the meal. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=OH8OX-zJoit3svaOB43TdA&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

Chocolate Temptation Hazelnut & Caramel ($18.00): Two bulbous dollops of my favorite sweets - yes, please https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=AlSL3GcqMvrP-vqjz94YnA&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw!

After Eight Baked Alaska ($24.00): A wonderful combination of mint and chocolate flavors after an initial flame show - yummy https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=aOfqEgxk6ytI-FVNAOiRRQ&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw!

SERVICE
Online reservations through OpenTable was a snap. When we arrived in the downstairs lobby, we were directed up the spiral staircase to the next level. Warmly greeted by a host, he quickly had someone show us to our table, provided menus, had water poured for us, and gave us time to settle in. Once we ordered, the rest of the evening was calm, relaxing, and not rushed at all as each drink and dish came out perfectly timed. The service was impeccable - cheers!

PARKING (Varied; N/A this instance)
About a 30-minute Lyft ride due to traffic from Jersey City. Otherwise, I didn't see any lots but believed there were random spots along the main drag of Madison Ave. and all surrounding streets as well as a plethora of nearby subway stations - 'nuff said.

ATMOSPHERE, DÉCOR, AMBIENCE
A posh somewhat cramped space (there was the main dining room https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=E6jUCExrNjatVn9B0N7Q5g&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw, a bar, a pool table room, and alcoves) heavily decorated with framed pictures https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=Ao9Ekur-fZwn44KAHxARtQ&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw that gave it an old rustic gentlemens club feel. Minimal natural lighting came through the windows while dim electric ceiling lights and table candles filled in the rest. I honestly couldn't recall any TVs nor background music. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=Jb0Qfms3M5H8_xYfzYY0sg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw

ATTIRE
I was dressed in a suit and dress shoes. Otherwise, business casual would be the bare minimum.

OVERALL
We had a lovely time at The Clocktower and would consider another visit. The drinks/food were very good, the fanciness was lost on me, the prices reasonably digestible, the service amazing, and the experience was fun to enjoy with others. I found very good value based on the prices, service, and experience noted above (TOTAL paid experience was around $245.00 BEFORE any discounts and/or tip). And, they accepted my credit card of choice... AMEX! 4.0 STARS

I requested a table for two by the window for my birthday. I made this request several times over the phone and by email. So they gave me a table for four in the middle of the room. Food is good though overpriced.
Okay food, terrible service. For the price, check elsewhere. Disappointed because the space was so cute.

So I dated a guy that seemed to have gotten a cheat cheat on how to chase me away. After two/three bad dates in a row, he finally took me here for a drink. Men, all us women in their thirties want is a nice place to drink cocktails. After you've snagged them, make them do things they don't like and such... Anyways, I recall the drinks being delicious here. I remember asking the guy what the name of the place was so I can go back one day. 

Fast forward to last week, a senior manager at my job who I got very close to was in town. Every time she is in town, she stays at the hotel this is located in so it just made sense to have dinner here. There was a very creepy old man that kept trying to squeeze into our conversation that sort of made me want to get the hell out of there as soon as possible, but everything else was good. We got the following.

- Celery like based soup: When the plate showed up, it showed up with a few mushrooms in the middle of a large plate. I had no idea what the heck that was and my senior manager and I looked at each other so confused. Then they poured the thick broth, which made so much more sense. It was a good laughing moment. The soup was fine, but I really didn't like the celery like flavor that lingered every bite. I didn't finish my soup to be honest.
- Crab cake: the creepy guy suggested this and I am grateful for his creepiness. This was delicious! Crispy based with crab in the middle. We shared this, but can easily have this on my own.
- Halibut: this was delicious! I love a good poached fish moment. 

Staff is good. They do up sale a lot which was a bit annoying. How much food can one eat at 7 pm on a Wednesday? I gave this place three stars because I feel like I haven't had a chance to really give their menu a try. What I had was good, but I am dying to try the beef wellington. Stay tuned for an updated review.

The food was Amazing we loved everything we ordered. Ambiance very classic and clean. 
We ordered two starters roasted beetroot salad and the scallops, scallops were fantastic. Prime NY stripe is a must we ordered medium rare and it was cocked to perfection. We didn't love the bourbon ice cream ( no flavor ) but their signature dessert 'warm sticky toffee pudding' was something else. The four stars are just because the wine by the glass list is very poor , the old fashioned was just not there ( you can't mistake an old fashioned in such fancy restaurant) and we would have expected the same level of service, our waiter was very very gentle and kind but I guess it was new and I think the management should have supported him more. There are basic mistakes that could have been avoided in a high end restaurant.

The food and ambiance is fantastic. We got oysters, steak tartare, the pork chop and the fish n chips. Every bite was delicious and they were playing groovy music. However, the service was horrible and it really impacted our experience. They may have just been understaffed on a Saturday night, but aside from when they first sat us down and took our drink orders we had to track down the waiter every time we wanted/needed something. It was clear everybody in the restaurant was experiencing this and you could overhear others complaining. They were also very slow to clear empty plates. I would go again but probably not on a Saturday or Friday night.

We were very disappointed. I came there to have the Beef Wellington. Which cost $62? The meat was fine, but there wasn't any patte. It was about 1/8 eighth of an inch, incredibly small. I asked for a a replacement and they said we can't, it's made this way. They did not try to make it up to us. It was very disappointing. I don't recommend. That you go there.

Came for a burger and of course ate other stuff too. Such a good burger though! And you know I am serious when it comes to burger perfection. This place is up there in my burger list. Menu is amazing overall. Try their Mac'n'cheese as an appetizer. I swear!

This place has been on my bucket list. They used to have one Michelin star. It is a London food restaurant. It was not too difficult securing a reservation during the holidays, which is great. It has beautiful interior and very romantic vibe. It has a pool table as well and a beautiful staircase that people take pictures at. We got beef Wellington, baked Alaska, fish and chips, Chicken Liver And Foie Gras Parfait, burnout cocktail, and this other grapefruit flavored cocktail. Super cool show with baked Alaska, so make sure to order that!! Beef Wellington was great and one of the dishes that they are known for!

The absolute worst experience I have ever had in a restaurant. The service was extremely bad. From not serving us water for about 30 min after we sat down to opening our wine and forgetting it on the counter and not pouring it for 15 min till we flagged someone down. We order appetizers and one of us did not have a plate for 10 min. The champagne was never refilled. The wine was never poured. The Mac and cheese for $20 had literally 5 rigatoni and water at the bottom. The waiter knew nothing about the dishes and had to ask about each one. The manager did not communicate to the waiters what she was telling us, resulting in us looking like we did not want to pay for food items that had been comped. Overall worst experience ever wasted our favorite Christmas holiday dinner on a place that once had a Michelin star and now has worst service than a fast food restaurant.

It's good, but not great, especially for a starred restaurant. Came here on a Tuesday night for a dinner with colleagues. Service was generally good, but they misheard one of our drink orders and brought us the wrong cocktail by mistake (we'd ordered a wine), and did not offer to take it off the bill. 

I don't remember what everyone else got, but I had the fluke chop. It was...okay. It had a lot of little bones.

Their dessert menu is pretty good, and they make a show about bringing out the baked Alaska and setting it on fire. 

I'm glad I went, but probably would not go back.

We came here late for a same-day dinner reservation and had a nice date, though an overall meh culinary experience. I wouldn't say I regret coming here, but definitely won't repeat. 


For our starters, the scotch egg tasted good, and it was a good scotch egg relative to what I've had in the US, but that bar is quite low. 

The maine scallop was probably my favorite dish. It was well seasoned and had some unique flavors, with the leak-cream sauce. It had a good number of scallops, but I felt that the texture of the dish was a bit one-note and very soft to really be enjoyable. 

The Foie Gras with Orange wasn't my favorite. I personally didn't find that the sweetness of the orange able to compliment the rich flavors of the food gras. I also think that the fish would have done better with some crispier bread. 

We had a beef Wellington as our main, which was the main reason we came here. I will say that it was perfectly cooked, but found it under seasoned. The sauce helped, but it didn't completely win me over. The potatoes were decent (as I would expect at any restaurant) but I felt that the bone marrow didn't really add anything to the meal. It kinda felt that the bone marrow was there to justify the cost of the meal, and it wasn't really additive. 


The drinks were quite good and the ambience of the restaurant were on par with what I would expect, though it was a bit ritzier than what I was expecting and felt underdressed.
We had pancakes and English breakfast. The service was good and the pancakes were very tasty. The English breakfast was a bit too greasy but overall a solid place with a nice atmosphere.

Came here for a private party and was very pleased with everything. The food was all delicious, particularly the steak. The private room decor is also stunning yet intimate. Will definitely be back to try the regular menu as well.

Excellent refined take on British fare in a beautiful setting that makes you feel like you are sitting in a dimly lit parlor.  The fare is wonderful - we enjoyed every single dish and I highly recommend trying the Beef Wellington and pork chop.  The meats are tender, flavorful, and perfectly cooked to a medium rare, and the accompaniments are the perfect foil.  I also would get a side of the oxtail mac and cheese, and the Shepherd's Pie, if you have stomach space.  The tandoori chicken is good but didn't really stand out.  

Service is fine - until it starts getting busy - and then you basically will need to do a tap dance to get anyone's attention.  Docking off a star for an otherwise 5-star experience.  We came for my birthday and that was noted on the reservation but pretty much ignored.

It's a good option in a beautiful hotel in Flatiron so worth a trek BUT come at an off-hour or you may be waiting a while for a very low-touch service experience that is not the norm at a Stephen Starr venue.

I really hate to rub salt on the wound, but I can kind of see why Clocktower lost its Michelin star. It LOOKS Michelin-caliber, but it certainly doesn't taste or feel Michelin-caliber.

My Celeriac Soup was gross. Pungent and bitter in a way that I didn't know celeriac could be, even with trumpet mushrooms thrown in. They presented it strangely too, placing the bowl with the ingredients down first, then taking 5+ min to retrieve the broth and pour it over said ingredients. We were so confused during those 5 minutes, wondering where our server had wandered off to, and also, was this some kind of dry, broth-less soup no one had ever heard of?

The other dishes were better, with the pork chops being the highlight of the night. Unfortunately, the service issues kept happening, culminating in our server bringing over 5 dessert menus for 6 people, completely overlooking our sixth person. When she asked why she hadn't been given a menu, he stammered a response that made it clear he just hadn't noticed her--even though she was sitting at the front of our table and was the closest to him. She was so upset at being forgotten, she asked to leave the dinner early--and we left with her in solidarity.

The restaurant is very Instagrammable in that old NYC money kind of way, and the well-dressed clientele certainly reflect that. But all the crown molding and EMP-neighboring in the world can't make up for poor acoustics that echo and amplify EVERY sound to the point of cacophony, making it absolutely impossible for a party of 6 seated in a corner to hear each other. Between that,  the service issues and the lackluster food, The Clocktower talks the talk but can't walk the walk.
Beautiful space. Exceptionally good service. Would return for after-show dessert/drinks.
Everything was super delicious. The ambiance at the restaurant was cool. Would love to go back again

I really love this place. Been here several times already. So happy it survived COVID. The freshly baked bread is always amazing. Really hope the apple tarte tatin can come back, it's one of the best desserts I've ever had

Came for brunch a few weeks ago and we had a great experience! The space is located upstairs from a hotel lobby so we had to go looking for it a bit. Brunch is located in a smaller dining area that the hostess led us to and it wasn't very crowded for a Sunday. Funny enough, we didn't really try the brunch food and stuck with the lunch options which were pretty good. The "Mac and Cheese" had great sauce and the meat melted in your mouth. That being said, it was not what I expected so putting that out there. The highlight of this meal was definitely the desert. We shared a crème brûlée with pina colada sorbet which turned out to be such a good combination. Brunch was good, but I would want to come back for dinner!

Went tonight for a friends birthday dinner and it was wonderful. We loved the food and highly recommend the Scotch Egg, Beef Wellington and Fish and Chips and the Sticky Toffy Pudding was perfect. The staff were excellent. The hostess who greeted us was lovely and our server and the bussing staff were so attentive and kind and truly made us feel welcome. The manager was superb, he took such great care to ensure we enjoyed ourselves and made it all so special from start to finish. We will definitely be returning and what a beautiful decor, comfortable with a nice vibrant energy from staff and guests.

Went into the city for dinner and show and chose the Clocktower which worked out very very well. We were able to get a reservation that night, just a little trouble with the name but the host was able to sort it out quickly. Fantastic food, great drinks, and great staff helping us get through the meal in time to catch the train back to NJ. Beef Wellington, Scotch egg, and baked Alaska, couldn't ask for a better meal.
Nice fine dining experience, great for a small or large group with professional staff and a great ambiance to unwind and relax

Judging off of quality:price, the Clocktower simply wasn't of value. 

With a higher standard of dress and ambiance, you would expect the food to match its allure.

Beef Wellington, Shepherd's Pie, Mac and Cheese, and the Scotch Egg.

Let me preface that none of the food tasted poor. It was quite the meal, but was definitely nothing extraordinary. For about $90/person with no alcohol, one would expect to be blown away. 

Scotch Egg was good. Well seasoned and cooked right, the sauce also complemented the dish well.

Mac and Cheese had several pieces of well cooked pasta in a watery, cheesy, and bitter sauce. Good pasta, but the overall flavor was lacking in my opinion. 

Shepherd's Pie was the highlight of the meal. Well-seasoned and the portion size was decent. Tasted delightful and we cleaned the plate nicely.

The Beef Wellington was OK. Cooked well, but not really seasoned. While eating it, the only thing we could taste was the dijon mustard followed by the rest of the dish. 

Highlight: attentive, kind, and fast service. 

Thank you to the staff who treated us well. $60+ Wellington was the knock-down for me, but the meal itself wasn't bad at all. 

Worth a try, but questionable to be a regular.

Scotch egg, Chicken liver foie gras parfait: both well executed and tasty

Mac & cheese with ox cheek: the twist on this dish is a delightful surprise

Beef Wellington: well executed with quality ingredients

Fish & chips: not bad, but somewhat mediocre (i.e. lack of creativity / style) compared to the other dishes

We went in the morning on Sunday for a light brunch. There were only 2 other tables besides us for most of the time. We somehow waited a full FORTY minutes before somehow took our order - the servers were just wandering around with vacant looks on their faces. It took them another 30 to bring our food.

The service here was despicable and I saw several other tables sitting there with confused and annoyed expressions on their faces. Truly awful (AND the food was mediocre).

started with amazing house made bread that was so good we got 2. oxtail mac and cheese was ungodly good. beef wellington, however, was lacking flavor and a little to rare for me. mushrooms were to dry. the bread pudding was very good and great presentation also.

Went there twice and both experiences were great! 
Service was good and the interior is beautiful. 
The Wellington steak or the Shepard' pie were just like what I had in England. 
Great place to chill at Friday night or weekend. 
With limited options for British food in NYC it's definitely a great one once crave for British cuisine!!!

Disappointing Brunch, took 45 minutes to bring 4 drinks at 11:30 am and no tomato juice for bloody Mary's only a mix . Food was good. It's nothing special..... 
The hotel itself is fabulous

As part of my mission to hit every single Michelin restaurant during my time in the NYC area, I finally checked out The Clocktower located next to Madison Square Park. First impressions were definitely positive with the sleek stairwell leading up the to the impressive ambiance of an old English sporting pub. I ordered the Scotch Egg to start which was essentially a small quail egg wrapped in some type of sausage (tasted like a maple breakfast sausage) and then battered and deep fried. Per the recommendation of my waitress, I ordered the popular Beef Wellington and I can honestly say it was one of the better variants of the classic dish that I've experienced in my life. However, as is mostly the case with other Michelin establishments I've tried, I was not too blown away by either the food or service. Definitely a high quality meal with great cocktails to accompany, and something everyone should at least try during their time here in the city.

Went here for my birthday dinner with my family. It is housed in the New York Edition hotel which is an actual clocktower on the 2nd floor.

My family wanted to take me somewhere that was nice but didn't obliterate the bank so we saw the menu here and decided to try.

We ordered the cabernet here to start it was very good, smooth and easy to drink. The sommelier came over to help us sort out a bottle.

We started off with the scotch egg with walnut ketchup. This was my first scotch egg and it was delicious! The walnut ketchup paired perfectly with it. Really enjoyed!

We then ordered starters which were the scallop and the crab cocktail tartine. The scallops were perfectly cooked and perfectly luscious. They were everything I wanted when biting into a scallop. The crab tartine was just so fresh and beauty of the delicious crab meat one the show but the whole piece of the tart helped get all the flavors to marinate that crab in the perfect bite.

For mains we ordered the fish and chips, the halibut in lemon butter, the lamb shepherds pie and the tandoori chicken with basmati rice. The fish and chips were so moist instead with a thin crispy batter. The fries were nice and thick cut and just perfect. The halibut was perfectly moist and the lemon butter sauce helped it just melt in your mouth. The lamb shepherds pie was divine. It's very rich but so uber flavorful, a must try. Lastly the chicken was delicious with the best basmati rice with herbs, dried fruit, pistachio and other accompaniments. One of the best rice I've ever had. 

For dessert we ordered the sticky toffee pudding and the strawberry tart. The sticky toffee pudding was sweet and everything tasted and was exactly ad described. The strawberry tart was the only item I could've done without. The strawberry was in a meringue and not a tart filled with pastry cream. The best part of that dessert was the strawberry gelato on the side.

This was a great experience with pleasant service, never felt rushed and great food. If the opportunity arose I would return.

The Clocktower was just all around amazing! My boyfriend and I got there 15 min. before our reservation and started off with drinks at the bar. The bartender was cool to talk with and the drinks were well made. There was also a pool table in an intimate room between the bar room and the dining room - wish we had known about it earlier!

The service was great and I really can't stop thinking about the food! We got the Chicken Liver & Foie Gras Parfait (snack), Crab Cocktail Tart (starter), Truffle Risotto (Main), Beef Wellington (Main), Strawberry Eton Mess (dessert), and Warm Sticky Toffee Pudding (dessert). I think the word crab just called out to me at first glance so I was stuck on it without really reading the other starter options haha. It was tasty, but I would definitely want to try the Seared Diver Scallops next time or the Berner's Tavern Macaroni and Cheese, which our waitress had recommended. We just didn't get it because we were already getting the Truffle Risotto, which was mouthwateringly flavorful. And the Beef Wellington was, of course, fantastic. Both our desserts were great, but the Warm Sticky Toffee Pudding was the winner! We realized towards the end that we didn't receive their bread and butter to start with but were too satisfied with everything else to mind haha. We did get complimentary glasses of champagne for our anniversary celebration :)

A solid choice in NoMad. Great space, great playlist, good cocktails and pleasant and efficient service. The food is consistently okay, though I have never had anything I thought I really needed to eat again.

This was probably the best English food I've had in NYC - bottom line.  Also the service was very attentive, the floor manager came over to check on our meal twice, which I appreciated.  This restaurant truly went above and beyond to exceed the high standards that it has set.  Ordered the scotch egg with house-made ketchup (9/10), the steak tar-tar (10/10), the truffle risotto (9/10 - a little too heavy on the Parmesan for my taste), the cheese burger with fries (8/10 - very good, but I would've preferred a bit of a drier burger), and the strawberry shortcake dessert (10/10).  I overheard another table compliment the fish and chips here, so I would definitely return to try that in the near future.  Also, the sourdough bread with salted butter was absolutely delicious!

Dinner at the 24K gold leaf bar was pleasant and the bartenders are pros. Started out with the Dill or No Dill cocktail, which was the perfect balance between sweet, salty, and herbaceous. For an appetizer, I chose the Chicken Liver and Foie Gras Parfait. Despite a lot of mixed reviews, this was my favorite treat of the night. The creamy, tart, sweet, meaty, mix of flavors was intoxicating. Perfectly toasted bread had me sweeping down through the bowl to get every last morsel. I thought about ordering another one, it was that good. Next up was the fish and chips. Let's start with the mushy peas. Literally the best I've ever had. Fresh tasting, and a hint of what I believe was nutmeg, had me hooked. The large piece of cod was perfectly fried and extra crispy. The downside here was the "triple cooked" chips which were not crispy at all. They tasted like baked potatoes. The seaweed tarter sauce just didn't work for me, I feel it lacked onion and a little sweetness.

It was a cold damp winter night. My wife... Ronda and I fell into a sinkhole earlier that night immersed over our head with no way out. We nearly S**t our pants! We mustard up the strength to climb our way out if this f*****g hole and when we got out, by golly were we hungry. We began walking around the city and stumbled upon The Clocktower. We have heard such good things about this place from fellow Yelpers and had to give it a try! We ate the Beef Wellington and it was good. 

-Ronald Crimpits ;

Exceptional Beef Wellington and probably the best Mushroom Risotto I've ever had! 
The interior looks amazing and the staff was friendly and attentive. 
I absolutely recommend this place and will be definitely coming back! 
P.S. my friends ordered a burger and fish and chips, I didn't get a chance to try it but it looked delicious:)
The breakfast took 50 mins on a regular Tuesday morning. We ordered fruits and oatmeal. That was unbelievably slow.

H and I wanted to try a one star Michelin Star restaurant in NYC. We found The Clocktower and immediately booked a table for two. The Clocktower is located in the New York Edition hotel by Marriott. The restaurant is beautifully designed. We got a very friendly server. The service was great. We asked for recommendation and we were recommended the duck special of the night. 

The duck special came with a duck liver pate onion pastry. The duck itself was nicely cooked and the outer layer skin was nice and crispy. It came with a generous side of duck glaze sauce to be poured onto the duck. Overall the food was very delicious. Our service for the night was wonderful. We had a great time. 

The decor of the restaurant was beautiful. There was a nice fireplace in one of the room. The color tone made the place stand out like a beautiful cozy livingroom. On the wall, there were many photos

I highly recommend coming here for dinner. You will not be disappointed.

I was looking for a special brunch for Mother's day.  I live nearby.  Every place I called said they had no reservations, and this place said the same.  However, they said I could come and try:  so we did.  It is in a new modern hotel and I had never heard of it, so I wasn't surprised that they had space when we walked in. 

I loved the vintage space.  As an old life-long New Yorker, I suspect that this space was a former private club.  There is mahogany and a fire place and it is dark and old school.  But I got the feeling that there is not enough of a celebration of the space, since that is really the draw.  No one mentioned it.  I didn't see anything printed about the history of the place.  I suspect that it is managed by people who are not familiar with its history.  

The food was above average.  The staff shares all tasks, which we had to figure out.  You can ask anyone for anything and don't have to wait for your waiter.  Had we known that, we would have had stellar service.  I am not complaining:  I think the waiter should have let us know.  In NY, you are sort of beholden to your waiter....

I would recommend it.  However, if it has a Michelin star, you couldn't tell today.

Went to The Clocktower for an anniversary, and we were not disappointed. The service was impeccable. Our waiter Michael was very attentive! As for the food and drinks, the highlights were the Mac and cheese, scallops, mushroom velouté and the quince cocktail. Great vibes all around!

PSA - Please don't waste your time with thIs restaurant. Clearly everyone knows this since it was empty on a Saturday night. To get an idea of what the menu tastes like please try taking a bite of a cardboard box covered with Heinz Hp sauce. I assure this won't change the perception that British food is terrible.

I had no idea this place had a Michelin star but I can see why. First, the design of the restaurant feels like you've stepped into the study or dining room of a viscount complete with a fireplace, soaring high ceilings and framed black and white photos on the wall. There is also a separate room for billiards and a bar with a beautiful curved bar and several other rooms for dining throughout. We sat near the big windows overlooking Madison Square Park and the lighting was so nice with the sun streaming in.

We came for brunch and ordered the scotch egg, burger and fish and chips. I was actually impressed with the scotch egg with walnut ketchup as it was served hot with the quail egg yolk perfectly medium. The burger was so tasty with the Churchill sauce and thinly sliced pickles and red onion and crispy bacon. The thick-cut chips were surprisingly huge and filling -- made me imagine how big of a potato they used! We were impressed by the proportion of the fish and chips. Perfectly battered and served with mushy peas (loved) and seaweed tartar sauce. Although we were so full, we decided to try the nutmeg creme brûlée and gobbled it up. There is definitely a strong nutmeg flavor (not my favorite) but they serve it with a yoghurt sherbet which cuts through. I would definitely come back to try the sticky toffee pudding and another table was being served a version of a baked Alaska which looked very delicious. 

Would love to come back for dinner and hoping for a more lively atmosphere as it was pretty empty for a Saturday brunch -- not a bad thing during Covid Times though.

Ordered the Burger, Risotto, Beef Wellington, Shepherd's Pie, and Scallops.  For dessert, the Baked Alaska and Sticky Toffee.

My favorites were the Burger and Risotto.  The Sticky Toffee was exceptional in flavor and presentation.

Shepherd's Pie was a little lackluster.  I expected something innovative, but it was a standard Shepherd's Pie.

Price is reasonable for a Michelin starred restaurant compared to others.  I would gladly come here again for the Sticky Toffee.

Went to The Clocktower last night for dinner and had the best dinner experience!  The food was delicious and the service was absolutely the amazing!  Thank you to our server Evan and the rest of the team that took great care to make sure we had everything we needed.  

P.s. Definitely finish up your meal with the sticky toffee pudding!

We went for brunch. I mean, it was alright. Great service I guess. But maybe thats what Michelin Star means. In terms of food, it was ok but super $$$$$. Just go to a diner instead and order to your heart's content
You have to go for the beef Wellington and Eccles cake (my mother in law is from Eccles so I'm bias, but the sticky toffee pudding looked amazing too)

Absolutely delightful. The ambiance and the food were beyond my hopes. It happened to be my birthday, and my server, Evan, treated me like a queen. The fish and chips were perfectly lovely. I really enjoyed my time here. I wish I lived closer but will definitely come again my next trip to the city.

Dark paneled ceilings and a large marble hearth aglow with flames created a welcoming and cozy ambiance.  My dining group of four decided to order and share 3 appetizers.  I'd never had a scotch egg before, but as someone who has an unhealthy love of eggs in all preparations I've ever tasted (I'm sure the two eggs I eat most mornings are not doing anything wonderful for my cholesterol level), I was sure I would enjoy this dish.  And I was correct.  The fried outer coating provided a satisfying crunch.  The savory yolk and pork sausage was cut by the acidity of the accompanying walnut ketchup.  We spoke to the sommelier to get his advice on wine pairings for each course.  He recommended a sparkling wine from the south of England to pair with the scotch egg.  It was right on point!  Note to self: anything fried goes well with bubbles. 

Next up, Berners Tavern macaroni & cheese with wild mushrooms and slow-cooked ox cheek.  This was not the usual elbow pasta with bright yellow artificial cheese from a box.  This was a bit of a masterpiece.  Large, hearty ribbon pasta noodles with meaty mushrooms and tender, flavorful ox cheek in a rich creamy sauce.  Absolutely delicious.

The final appetizer was chicken liver and foie gras parfait.  Although savory, it was not the richest foie gras I've ever had.  Nevertheless, the perfectly toasted brioche bread with a soft center was the perfect vehicle for foie gras.

On to the main course, the beef wellington, the dish I was most excited about.  Admittedly, my first bite was a bit lackluster.  The meat seemed a bit dry and under seasoned.   However, I quickly learned that the remedy lay in the mash potatoes and gravy that accompanied the dish.  Combining all the elements of the plate on my fork, the perfect bite highlighted the interplay of textures between the flaky outer pastry and mash potatoes, and allowed the savory gravy to add flavor and moisture to the beef.  Overall I was quite pleased.

We capped the evening with a delicious warm sticky toffee pudding

We had good service throughout the night and any small snafu was quickly addressed; great customer service.  I would definitely dine here again.

Food was amazing. Staff was amazing. Drinks were amazing. It's a very selective menu so keep that in mind before going and it's definitely on the pricey side. The ambience is cute too. We decided on here as we were staying at the hotel and a snow storm was in effect. Overall great experience

Super fun michelin spot turning out British goodies on a high end scale - I will say - BEST COCKTAILS I HAVE HAVE EVER HAD- Leo our server was also awesome, they never judged when we asked for more bread butter even the black salt on our cocktail ! The beef Wellington is a must as it's so time consuming and nice to have it prepared right ! Fish and chips were nice but not necessarily mind blowing - the salad was DELICIOUS! And malted chocolate ice cream was a lovely treat - interior is stunning and just so fun !

My husband took me here for our 1 year wedding anniversary. Meal was wonderful! The wine som was super friendly and very attentive. Our waiter was a little quiet but was always on top of things. Fantastic meal all around. We did the Mac and cheese for a starter & I had the shepherds pie and he had the beef Wellington. Great bread and butter service too.

Went here two weeks ago and had a really good time!  The interior was beautiful and if you have time, play some pool.  The food was all memorable, but portions were huge so keep that in mind.  The mac and cheese was so creamy and the ox cheek melts in your mouth. The shepard's pie had the type of taste where you can't stop eating once you dig in.  The fish and chips were so nicely prepared.  I grew up eating beer battered fish from my mom, so I was very fond of the fish, but the ale they used was so tasty I loved the crust.  The dessert also had some gold flakes which was really nice.  Highly recommend!

Hickory dickory dock.
This place was quite a shock.
The Mac and cheese was good.
Could the Scotch egg be better? It could.
Hickory dickory dock.

We made a res for 7:45 but they didn't seat us until 8:15, which was a bit unfortunate since we were all feeling quite peckish.  Also service in general was quite slow. 

FOOD:  The Mac and cheese with oxtail was actually really tasty, as was the dry aged burger.  I also tried the scallops, a bite of the beef Wellington, and the lamb shepherd's pie.  

The shepherd's pie was really strong and rich, and there was a lot of it. We ate around 1/4 of it and packed up the rest to bring home. I wish there were other things (maybe as a side) that would have cut into the richness. The balance just felt a bit off overall.  Others really enjoyed the scallops, but I thought they were just ok. Same with the beef Wellington, but I also am not a huge fan of filet mignon in general. 

I overall thought this place was nice, but expected a bit more from a Michelin starred restaurant.
Super cute British style restaurant. Great energy and fun vibe for a special occasion.

I was only in town for a night when I spotted The Clocktower on IG, they had me at Lamb Shepard's Pie. Sold immediately, I grabbed my coat and headed out. Parking was available on the street and I got a spot right up front. The restaurant is located in the Edition hotel so the lobby area was really cool, I grabbed a picture at the stairway and headed up. The decor inside the Clocktower was amazing. The Shepard's pie was perfectly seasoned I literally ate the whole thing in less than 10 minutes. Very well deserving of the Michelin Star 
 Lamb Shepard's pie 

Instagram.com/six10_1984

Though this is a MICHELIN STAR RESTAURANT I honestly EXPECTED MORE. The WEST COAST OYSTERS WERE PHENOMENAL & The FRESHLY BAKED BREAD was the star of the show. The burger on the other hand, the main reason we went there, was LESS THAN SPECTACULAR. The service was IMPECCABLE, as expected. The staff was very well trained and attentive ; they came in between courses and CLEANED OFF THE TABLE  & changed the utensils which is always something you want to see at this level of dining. When it came to the desert, I really really enjoyed the JASMINE TEA. Very DISTINGUISHED from the usual jasmine tea I have at home.

Must Haves :

* Berners Tavern macaroni and cheese
* Dry Aged Burger ( Still worth trying )
* West Coast Oysters

This was my first visit to a Michelin star restaurant and it lived up to every bit of the hype.

We started with the butternut squash soup and I want to fill a bathtub with it now.

Entrees were amazing! 

I decided to splurge and get the Earl Grey soufflé. I was nervous at the $20 price point, but then I ate it and would have given them $30. 

The staff really helps make this a Michelin star place. They treat you like you are royalty. 

Please find a way to make this place a stop. They deserve all of the love.

This is a great place. Other five star restaurants can't compare. This is a one Michelin star place and they deserve it. The architecture and ambiance is enough of a reason to to go, the food is just a bonus. The spiraling staircase is a great photo op, so take plenty. 

We heard a rumor that they have the best fries. We didn't get them when we went but we will definitely come back for them. The food we did order, however, was fantastic. There isnt anything in their menu we don't want to try. 

The only issue we had when we were there was the waitress forgot to refill our coffee after we asked twice.

I went to The Clocktower for my birthday, and they were all SO nice!

Everything was very good, except for the skate wing, which neither of us liked very much. However, the service was phenomenal, and all the other dishes were great.

You can also play pool after dinner. There is a separate room.

I only want to eat here for team/business lunches from now on. The environment was incredibly pleasant, beautiful, and comfortable. I ordered off the restaurant menu with skepticism because quality goes down in most places during these promotions - but not here! Loved it all and will be back. Especially for dessert.

2/14/20 our valentine day is a special thing for us. I surprise my lady to this restaurant since she been wanting to come here. When we first came in to the restaurant the vibe was nice and really fancy. However, they change the menu on the day of valentine day without letting us know ahead of time in their website. It was $136 per person for 6 courses. The first course was 2 oysters. The 2nd was fish which my girlfriend was not a fan of it. We told the waitress if we can Substitute but she said " are you allergic"? My girlfriend said "no" but she does not eat fish at all. Then the waitress just ignored it. The 3rd course it did come until 45 mins like literally 45 mins. In addition to that it was really cold inside and our legs were numbing from it. There was a draft of cold coming in behind us. My girlfriend was wearing dress so she was extra cold. The person who sat next to us who was pregnant complain how cold it was to the waitress then she said "aww you're cold" what's? Like for a fancy place like that you don't have heat? Then 4th course came to our table which was very tiny and they added some extra flame to make it look fancy but when you eat it, it taste like gas and alcohol nail polish remover. Then we waited for another 20 mins For the other food to come. It was ice cream and something else very satisfying. Then after that a tall guy with a suit I think he was the manager give us a check but we realized they only give us 5th course. Not 6th. A lot of waiter and waitress was running around looking so busy but forget to attend to there customer. Then we complain how they didn't give us our 6th course. Waitress apology but not very polite and the waiter came with the food with attitude and slam the plate in the table. 

Overall: for a fancy and very expensive place like this it is not worth of coming specially the customer service really suck. The food take way to long to come. We were cold because we sat next to the big window no one took care of it. They forgot our 6th course like how? I thought the people were way to professional? We thought wrong. We were having a good time because we have each other but the experience itself being there it's a mission because we got tired of sitting and waiting. We were there for almost 3 hours. Deeply in our feeling we wanted to leave but we didn't wanna ruin our night. The totally was $$$$. Definitely not recommend and I will be sharing this to my audience as well. 

Instagram: @Kenexplorer 
Google guide level 7.

Came here for a couple of quick drinks. Sat at the bar with a friend at lunch time. The service was great and prompt. I got the American cereal cocktail and it was nice and punchy. It came in an awesome/cute glass as well. Also ordered the buttermilk fried chicken. So nice and tender I couldn't stop myself from demolishing it. 4 drinks and chicken tenders were $100 with tax and tip. There's also a pool table there in case anyone is interested in playing. Cocktails cost circa $18-20 each.

Had dinner there last night. Service is shockingly horrible. 
To start off my friend and I were seated in a hurry as though all tables might be immediately taken.
Our server appeared and disappeared sparingly. He had never inquired of foods allergies, water type preferences or anything of that nature. He never bothered to check in on us. When I inquired about oyster types, he had no idea what kitchen was offering. When we asked about the $115 tasting menu, his answer was "4 courses".
We had to wait for a while to get our water glasses refilled. 
Menu wise , it is a combo of innovative and shwanky, yet the presentation piece is missing. 
I opted for a burger for my main. It was delicious although I am not a big meat lover. Fries were cold. I asked the  bus boy to bring new fries out, which took forever. I wound up eating my burger with no fries. 
My friend and I shared a side of wild mushrooms, which were very very salty.
I will not come back ever!!!! I recommend everyone and anyone looking for a delicious fancy meal to take their  business elsewhere.

Very unique, they have a Sommelier cart among other interesting attributes. Dishes are pretty solid. Only thing I didn't like was the meat being kind of burned but I think that's how it's supposed to be

I had never heard of this place until last night but my friend booked it for a birthday dinner for a dear friend. It was located in a part of town I don't frequent as much and tucked away in what I think was a hotel. Very nixe decor inside with lots of cool art.

Service was great. We ordered many different oysters, scallops, Mac and cheese and salad.

Tried the Lancaster chicken and Burger which I had and they were both amazing. 

So many food desserts we went with the pear pie and it was super tasty.

Great place to go for a special occasion, date and a great meal.

This place is a must go to! The venue is warm, embracing, old school all about old nyc. The service is impeccable and well the food... there is nothing on the menu that is bad. I have to say they have best Mac n cheese I ever ate! Been here for dinner and lunch and both time did not disappoint.
Also I love the bar area upstairs attached but separate ... great place to grab a delicious drink after or before dinner

A lot of hype over the Michelin star restaurant. The service was great but the food was OK- I honestly expected more for the price/hype/reviews. The bread was out of this world but the other portions of our meal fell short on our expectations. I am sure there are plenty of other places in NY with better food.

Very Disappointing. We had dinner reservations for Christmas Day, there was no Christmas ambiance or feeling. Very cold and uninteresting to say the least. The food was slow in coming out, it felt like the kitchen was overwhelmed. I know restaurants offer prix fixe menus on certain holidays but this was Not worth the time. There was nothing special or tasty about the food. I'll have to make better plans on my next holiday meal.

- Hella expensive
- But its worth the splurge
- My favorite drink was the cereal killer. It tasted just like alcoholic cereal
- The $100 steak didn't taste very $100 worthy, but I can say I did it
- Everything is delicious, and plentiful
- I love the potatoes
- I really just came here to tell you about the cereal killer. It's unlike anything you ever had, or will ever have

Service was so incredibly rude!! Have never felt so unwelcome in a restaurant. We came for a celebratory evening.
