The waiter rushed us through the entire meal, would start speaking and just turn away, never asked how we were doing and brought us the check before asking for desert. He then asked us 3 times if the check was ready. Meanwhile we'd only been there for an hour. If

If the meal is reserved, and your paying 35 dollars for drinks, note to the staff: don't push people out.

We absolutely loved the afternoon tea. 

I had no idea what to expect as I had never done something like this before. Would it be stuffy? Pretentious? Boring?

None of the above!

We sat down in a fabulously decorated room and was immediately attended to by a fun waiter who gave us just the right amount of attention the whole time. Only a few tables were populated so the setting felt very intimate. 

The tea selection was varied and thankfully included a couple non-caffeinated varieties. The tea was accompanied by a healthy amount of savories, sweets, and honeys. All were appropriate for a proper afternoon tea and were clearly made with attention to detail.

I would 100% recommend the afternoon tea experience if you or your loved one is into it. Worth every penny.

Must try the Oysters & Daikon-Uni-Caviar appetizer! As oyster connoisseurs who enjoy oysters often, I still don't understand how their oysters are 100 times better than all other oysters served at restaurants. Would love their sauce recipe for the oysters too. The Daikon-Uni-Caviar appetizer deserves an award. We literally want to serve it to guests at our wedding. Cocktails are very well made. The entire place is stunning. HIGHLY recommend.

I came here with my girlfriend for the Thanksgiving Prix fixe dinner.  The stairs to the restaurant remind me of an actual Clock Tower. But strangely I was hoping there will be actual clocks at the restaurant, but there were mainly just pictures.

Food: The food was really good specifically the Scallops and the New York Stripe (which was an additional $20).  What we both really liked was the free bread that they gave us in the beginning.  The bread was so hot but so soft on the inside while it came with homemade butter.  

Service: The service was good and perfect in my opinion as they were quick and efficient.

Overall: I would come back here to try their usual menu.
Ah, The Clocktower. If you want a moment to last a lifetime, eat here. It's the definition of excellent ambiance. That's all.

Amazing ambiance. Feels like you walked into a private club. Wood burning fireplaces. Leather chairs. Menu is simple and interesting.  Our table shared the tartare, the shepherds pie, a steak and the skate wing and a dandelion salad. All really yummy. The only downside at the restaurant was the wine list.  The average price for a simple bottle was close to 300.  Really dumb and such a turnoff.  It's easy to put a bunch of overpriced wines on a menu. It's much more interesting to find wines between 100 and 200.   Completely turned me off and didn't seem in line with the vibe.
I refrain from bad reviews but feel compelled to share. Underwhelming food, over priced and by far the worst service. Won't be back.. despite being Michelin star.

The Clocktower was a perfect place to take my very chic and glamorous mother to dinner.  She lives on Fifth Avenue on the UES, so she is suspicious of going downtown, where I live.  But Clocktower gave us a perfect table right in front of the fireplace, and she was charmed.  
The dining room feels like you're in an exclusive London club...  Oil paintings of horses and dogs cover the walls.  The food is beautiful and delicious.  
The service is elegant and smart.  They know what you need before you know it.
Wonderful dinner.  Expensive and worth it...

Kim Stanley Robinson's book "New York 2140" was set on this square and I thought it would be fun to eat here just for that -- but the restaurant is such a unique place with truly superb food -- mixing interesting flavors and doing it with great skill (I can make an excellent steak at home -- I want something more interesting than that when I go out), that I couldn't recommend it more highly. Although, the lamb chop was as classic as it gets -- and perfect in flavor and texture. For me, the desserts were where the food reached the 5th star, mixing meringue and chamomile or another time a pear torte that was flavored with something I have forgotten now, but made the pears more pear-like and not just the pear tart we all expect. Lovely staff, fun cocktails, delicious and interesting food.

I came here with my friends on a super rainy Wednesday night. My wonderful friends insisted on having a belated celebration here. Excited at first but we became tired and soaked; our mood was beaten down. 

But the service at this British fine dining Stephen Starr restaurant literally turned us 180! 
The ambiance was dark and romantic but in a way felt business casual. The dark red/brown furniture really gave us that English feel to it. The staff provided top notch service. Saying happy birthday every now and then while presenting with a birthday card, wine, and dessert on the house. Thank you so much for the surprise birthday mousse. You guys made the night even more special! 

I'm not your fine dining type of gal, but I loved every single dish we ordered. 

My favorites were definitely the scallops and their unique take on mac 'n' cheese (not heavy at all like American ones). It had ox cheek and mushrooms - SO delicious, you must try it.
The cod was so light and delicate.
The quinoa roasted chicken was beautifully presented.
Their skirt steak was cooked just right and paired with a delicious mushroom ketchup.
The apple crumble dessert was beautiful; a light sweet finish. Again, it's not like your heavy American version. A true delightful pastry art.

This place definitely lives up to its Michelin star. Will definitely be coming back!

Excellent spot for drinks with an interesting cocktail menu and fancy looking purple pool table. The service was quick! Just wish there was more seated space as those precious spots were quick to go. This is a place for one or two cocktails before moving on with the rest of your night.

I loved my first experience at The Clocktower.  I've been dying to go here considering I work close by.  I went during lunch and it was fabulous!
I would love to experience dinner.
The bread is amazing, warm and the butter is delish.
They stop by with amazing sweets at the end and I appreciated the portions.
I had the Basil Tagliatelle and it was so delicious.  Patrons aside me were enjoying their steak that smelled divine.  So, I'll be sure to dine here for dinner.

This is a fabulous place. The food was superb. The risotto was the best I've ever had. The service was outstanding.  We were celebrating and they gave us complimentary champagne and chocolates. Very nice ambiance. Everyone was so nice and attentive. I loved our dinner there. Strongly recommend.

I came here for dinner and was able to get reservations quite easily on OpenTable as I was staying at the Edition for work. 

I got the filet mignon and it was delicious and cooked perfectly with a hot pink center. The steak also doesn't come very thick, which was a pleasant surprise making it easier to cut through. 

Although the steak was good, I was unimpressed with the chilled asparagus side it came with. I think the asparagus would've definitely tasted better more cooked. Appreciated the fact that they were all asparagus spears though. 

Service was okay. It did seem like it took a bit for the food to come out. The servers are all extremely professional.

Given the location and price, overall it's just okay... 2.5 star probably. 

Service was meh, everytime the server put down new plates and took away the used ones they made a lot of noise.. Not gentle and as a "targeted fine dining" restaurant, it's not acceptable. The only proper one was the sommelier. 

It was a meal that we left with already forgetting what we ate. Nothing was really memorable. 

Appetizer -

East and West Coast Oysters $24 : okayed. 

Chilled Maine Lobster $32 : my favorite app, fresh and perfectly poached. Tasty flavors. 

Santa Barbara Uni $20 : not worth it

Marinated Mackerel $21 : not worth it

Roasted Maine Scallops $28 : okayed. 

Entree -

Day Boat Cod $39 : pretty good and nice flavor. 

40 Day Dry Aged Prime Côte de Boeuf $155 : not bad, acceptable but I doubt there's 32oz..

Long Island Duck Breast $44 : pretty good, acceptable duck. 

Roasted Loin of Lamb $47 : two pieces of lamb that was super gamey even people who eat lambs thought was too much. Yike!

Loved my first experience at The Clocktower! I went on a short lunch break for my birthday that my manager took me to. Unfortunately we didn't have a ton of time or we would have ordered more courses but what we had was great. 

The sourdough bread they bring out is delicious and perfectly hot out the oven. For my meal I ordered the pan seared cod which was so delicious I was spooning the sauce into my mouth like soup when the fish was gone. My boss had the burrata salad which was quite good. Word of note is that the portions are quite small for the price but very good. 

They brought me out a chocolate cake for a birthday dessert that was really good, and finished us off with scottish shortbread and English toffee treats that were delicious. 

The ambiance is really cool with a beautiful bar and billiard room and gold picture frames all around. This is a great spot for a business lunch or happy hour.

From the uncomfortably quiet and empty dining room to the embarrassing service, this is the first Michelin-starred establishment that has caused me to reconsider the integrity of Michelin rankings and make me wonder just who it is that has to be bribed to get these stars.  The Clocktower will make me take pause before considering any other one star from here on out. To be fair, I had the Afternoon Tea service, rather than dinner or lunch, but if you're open during those hours, you must meet your guests' expectations.  The Clocktower, on the other hand, clearly views 3-5pm from Friday to Sunday as an opportunity to slack on food and service, and as a ripe opportunity to bilk $55 from their guests on a pre fixe "Afternoon Tea" service.

Now, I've never had a proper "Afternoon Tea" in the British style, but I thought the prospect was intriguing at the very least.  Fancy little munchies, teas of various sorts (of which I know very little), and just the right amount of pretension in the air could make the whole ritual enjoyable, or maybe, as Wikipedia even put it, "taken as a treat in a hotel" after a particularly busy week.  The Clocktower, which offers "tastes of contemporary London" just steps away from Madison Square Park according to its website (not to mention the whole Michelin star thing) seemed like the perfect place to make my initial foray into pretentious Anglophile tea sipping.  

I could not have been more wrong.

The visit started off well enough, finding the admittedly gorgeous spiral staircase in the more vibrant downstairs bar area of the hotel and being greeted by name by the host.  Once seated in the ghost town of a dining room, we received the pre fixe menu consisting of your expected Afternoon Tea fare; various sandwiches, biscuits, jams, and the like.  There were a number of teas to choose from as well.  We immediately noticed that my guest and I had two different tea menus; no big deal, I would have never known about the Earl Grey option had I dined alone, but I opted for the White tea ($5 supp) anyway.  Still, odd that a place that has a Michelin star doesn't have conforming menus.  It's fine dining, not *Applebee's Daily Lunch Special.  

Once the food made it to the table (which felt like an eternity given we didn't have any choices to make, but in a large, silent room with only one other table of guests, could have been an acceptable wait) we immediately noticed that the sandwiches didn't match what was on either of our menus (presumably there is a different, third menu that neither of us received where all the sandwiches come on white bread and the desserts are just a series of question marks).  We asked the server about this discrepancy, who insisted on checking the menu with us (presumably in the event we couldn't read the word "pumpernickel" or didn't understand that pumpernickel, wheat, and rye breads all looked different than white bread), and had no real explanation.  Ok, then.  

Moving on to desserts, I couldn't even tell you what we ate.  Just look at the menu description and look what was served on the little tiered thing.  Do you see any tarts? (tart - a baked dish consisting of a filling over a pastry base). How about anything remotely resembling a sandwich? Me either. Given the experience with the sandwich bread situation, I didn't bother asking what the desserts were.  I'm just grateful I don't have a food allergy; the Clocktower would be a VERY dangerous place to eat. On top of everything else, as others have noted, it took quite some time to find a server to ask for the check.

This was not an Afternoon Tea experience by any stretch of the imagination; this was a way for the Clocktower to repackage old food as Afternoon Tea hors d'oeuvres and trick you into paying $55 for what would otherwise be their garbage (the gastrointestinal distress that followed from eating their aged seafood sandwiches support this theory). 
The servers (and the kitchen for that matter) have no idea what the menu says or offers; there is no "experience" whatsoever (aka explanation of the tea, the food, the ritual, etc.); and the entire thing takes place in an uncomfortably large and silent dining room.  Unless you're into having tea at the Hotel California (but with worse food, no Eagles song, and nothing supernatural about it), this place probably won't be for you.   

*this is an unfair insult to Applebee's, whose staff is often quite familiar with the specials.

(4.5/5)

An absolutely gorgeous venue (designed similar to its sister restaurant in London, Berners Tavern at the London EDITION hotel) that delights each and every time. From the start the service is lovely and attentive without being overbearing. The drink selection is impeccable (if pricey.) The room lulls you into a sense of comfort and the delicious and beautifully presented food seals the deal. I started with the tomato salad, which was light and perfect. The tomatoes were lush and acidic, adorned with a basil oil that was the ideal pairing. I then moved on to the 40 day aged NY strip steak, which was frankly one of the most tender, juicy, and perfectly cooked steaks I've had in a long time. I also sampled the cold asparagus side dish which was a refreshing antidote to the heaviness of the steak. Others at the table had the skirt steak, the foie gras appetizer, and the burger which is one of the best in town. The chips (I tried one) are fantastic.

I truly love this restaurant. A personal favorite I'd be happy to come back to time and time again.

Recommend it! The ambience is amazing! It's absolutely one of the best ambience in NYC. We ordered the tasting menu, which is not available on the website. It's $155 fix menu per person. It has four courses, and I love the scallops. However, the main course is duck, not the steak....

(4.5 stars) We came here after trying to catch up at a rooftop bar but it was way too crowded on a Friday night. They have very unique cocktails and a beautiful lounge space despite being located in the lobby of the Edition hotel. There's a beautiful spiral staircase that I wish I had climbed because now I will not know where it leads to! Imagine sitting in a quiet, dimly lit lounge with minimal square and rectangular furniture by candles and a fireplace. The shape of the lounge as it wraps around the elevators can make it hard to flag down a server but the service was okay. My cocktail even had the face of a clock atop my favourite egg white. The clock is edible as it is made of squid ink and rice paper!

Good looking and tasty food.
We went there for a work lunch and all food we ordered was good.I am removing one star for the service.The service was slow and our server was not attentive at all.

A wonderful visit. On top of all. the service was amazing. The Gentleman serviced us with warm smile and professionalism throughout the dinner. Each course was introduced and explained with details. 

The appetizer was absolutely delightful. We ordered foie gras and chicken liver Parfait. The presentation was innovative and upscale. The parfait came with a sour taste which was really appetizing.
 
I got the lamb for entree. The taste was well-balanced. Lamb was perfectly cooked: juicy, tender, and flavorful.
Nonetheless, the portion of my entree could be a bit bigger, considering my friend's duck breast came with two sides and mine came with one.

Loved the chocolate at the end of the dinner.

A really pleasant journey overall and would come again for special occasion.
Love this place - beautiful space, beautiful food and amazing service!  Great spot for business lunch.

Amazing dinner.  Beautiful old world steakhouse vibe with unparalleled service.  For appetizers fresh oysters, foie gras, and steak tartar were absolutely phenomenal.  The presentation was just beautiful as well.  I had the cod which was to die for.  Amazing wine selection and as well, and for sure get the bread!!  For dessert we had corn soufflé which takes a few minutes to make, but is well worth it.  Would be a great special occasion spot.

Went here for a work diner. We had a great time! The pork chop dish was definitely the best. Cocktails and wine list were amazing. The service was a little slower than my liking but overall a good experience.

Good food, but the menu seemed a bit heavy for summer. Service was was great with very personable staff.  The restaurant decor and ambiance is also quite beautiful, but I am not sure why, after we complained about the room being a bit warm, they turned up the ac but also lit the fireplace. . . odd

The food was excellent, but service was disenchanting. I dropped in for a late lunch post-room checkout and pre-flight, when the restaurant was sparsely occupied with only two other tables. Our server informed us that they had run out of the Beef Wellington. No problem - I opted for the skirt steak with chips instead. This is when the experience started going downhill: 

-30+ minutes after polishing off the appetizer, we were still twiddling our thumbs waiting for the steak to arrive. When we inquired about the status with our server and explained that we had a flight to catch, he nonchalantly responded, "Oh, I didn't realize you guys had somewhere to go." Um, okay. Since when did a 30 minute lag between courses without prior warning or proactive status update become acceptable?

-When another server placed delicious-looking fries on our table to accompany the steak, the main server told him that those weren't for us, and that our steak comes with the salad instead. At the time, I was a bit confused by this but didn't argue due to the time constraint. However, I'm positive that I had specified "chips" with my order. In fact, I had been craving those amazing looking golden wedges, but sadly could only stare at our neighboring tables devouring them. 

-After asking for the check, we placed our credit card in the holder immediately. Knowing we were now pressed for time due to the slow service, the server continued to meander around until we flagged him down. 

I only hope to live in a world of idleness and leisure like our server one day.

I was staying at the New York EDITION hotel and decided to come down for lunch. And I'm so glad I did - the food was wonderful.

To start, I had the complimentary sourdough which was AMAZING. I literally wanted to buy a few more to take with me to-go.

I opted for the 2-course lunch for which I chose the beef tartare and the sauteed skate, which were both lovely. The beef tartare was fresh and well-seasoned. The skate was cooked to perfection with the top still crispy.

I was on a conference call / working on my laptop and the staff were super understanding and helped me rearrange the table to put the food down. The ambiance / decor are a little old-fashioned looking, but overall, would highly recommend this place!

After having a lovely ($400) dinner, then waiting five minutes for an elevator that never arrived, my husband and I decided to walk down the poorly lighted circular marble stairway to the ground floor. I didn't see the last step and fell flat on my face. In pain and trying to pull myself together from the shock of falling, waitresses repeatedly stepped over me on their way in and out of the kitchen never offering to help or asking other employees (i.e. the manager or doorman) to assist us or inquire if I needed medical attention. Watch out for that last step, it's a doozy. And if they've already charged your credit card for the meal, don't expect any further interaction.

Inventive and well presented dishes but hit-or-miss taste wise. I was expecting more consistency and palate pleasing for the price, nonetheless a good meal and experience. The ambiance is sophisticated but not stuffy wasn't too formal - dark wood, large leather chairs, soft lighting, not too dark. I'd give it another shot if in New York.

Sourdough - Good flavor and warm from the oven.
Mac and Cheese - Fresh and firm pasta in a creamy, rich sauce. Oxtail was cooked well and extremely tender and flavorful.
Scallops - Soft texture, like cutting through butter. The soup it was in was slightly nutty.
Chicken liver foie gras terrine - Bitter and more acidic than I thought and the brioche was kind stale tasting. The texture was heavy and thick.
Duck - Fatty rich, not over cooked or gummy, pear was also nice
Chicken salad - Pickled vegetables were intensely vinegary, while the chicken was basic or dry cut medallions. The sauces were a nice intermediary but the whole dish didn't really come together.
Lobster - Quite good with the butter.
It's an elegant place for dinner with my girl. Nice experience and nice wine list. I ordered the steak and Foie Gras.
Swanky, sexy, delicious, decadent, fun. Don't miss the salad, the fois gras, the cocktails--it's all pretty perfect. This may become a regular spot for me on business trips.
Wonderful cuisine in an elegant rabbit warren of spaces tucked away in a high rise above Madison Park. The filet mignon is top notch!

Did not know what to expect, but definitely not disappointed! The duck breast was so tender and one of the best we've eaten. Had the tilefish which was moist and flaky. The sides were perfectly prepared. The sommelier chose a great French white wine, so light and perfect with our meal. Highly recommend this place. It's on the second floor of the Edition Hotel.

Not only was the food delicious but the outstanding hospitality we received from the general manager will be another selling point for recommending The Clocktower to all my friends & family. 

Love: Foie Gras & Chicken Liver Parfait (starter), Berners Tavern Macaroni & Cheese (starter), Whipped Potatoes (side), Dry Aged Burger (main), Beet Cured Heritage Pork Chop (main), Prime Filet Mignon (meat), Treacle Tart (dessert)

Like: Santa Barbara Uni (starter), 40-Day Dry Aged Prime NY Strip (steak)

Okay: Brooklyn Burrata (salad), Baby gem lettuce (side), Chilled Green Asparagus (side)

I have never been so disappointed by every single dish at a restaurant, is it my bad ordering or The Clocktower just has terribly underwhelming food?! Thank your waitstaff for their impeccable service for the two stars. 

Hudson Valley Foie Gras and Chicken Liver Parfait (0/5) - for being the biggest fan of foie gras I barely touched this dish because it is SO SALTY, when we asked for bread it took 20 minutes for the kitchen to prep it.. by then I was over this dish
Eggs Benedict (1/5) - just look at the photo I uploaded, is this not the saddest/most pathetic/underwhelming plate of eggs Benedict you've ever seen? Your corner deli can do a better job than this
Chocolate cake (1/5) - extremely dry cake, no thank you

The Clocktower is a perfect third date restaurant.  It's the private eating club that you're invited into tonight.  Get cozy with a drink in the plushy chairs while feeling like you're in someone's luxurious mansion.  This restaurant is on the second floor of the Edition Hotel on Madison Square Park.  It's gorgeous, has several rooms, including a pool table, and has pictures hung all throughout the vaulted ceiling rooms.  Even walking into the clock tower, you pass through the Edition lobby, with its Aspen fireplaces and fur throw blankets. 

The restaurant is based on a upscale British Tavern (if that tavern had gorgeously high ceilings and was well groomed). The food too is slightly English, including pigeon pie, fish and chips, and halibut.  However, you can find most classic light american dishes on there too, such as oysters,

The Clocktower:
Second time here. Top 3 brunch with Bessou and Buvette.
Recommendations:
1. Earl grey souffle 
2. Beef Wellington
3. Lobster salad
4. Crab toast with uni
You can order the earl grey souffle for weekend brunch if you email the restaurant before arrival. Great service!

Overall ambience is nice and the bar area is great but that's where it starts and ends. Had appetizers and entrees. Beef tartare was bland at best. The sliver of lamb priced at $46 was tough and not satisfying. The duck was ok. I was truly excited to try this place and then promptly disappointed.

I really loved how low-key and old school the vibe was at Clocktower, and for a Michelin-starred restaurant the experience was blessedly down to earth.

Our table only really shared two things: the Boston Lobster salad, and the 32 oz Dry Aged Ribeye ($160 or so). The Lobster salad was delicious, and quite fresh, if not particularly mind-blowing.

The steak though--what a treat. Easily shared between 3-4 people (which makes it downright affordable in this city), it was simply one of the best cuts of meat I have had in a while, and came with (!) a drool-worthy bone marrow jus, fantastic potatoes au gratin, and a decadent green bean and truffle salad. 

I barely had any room for dessert, but we went for the Earl Grey soufflé and I'm glad we did. It was light, delicious, and a perfect way to end the meal.

It was kind of weird to go in expecting a stuffy, Michelin-style experience and end up finding my new probably-favorite steakhouse in the city, but it was a pleasant surprise. I'll definitely be back to try some of their other entrees too, if I can convince myself to skip the steak. Easier said than done...

The bartender made me some amazing tequila cocktails (no margarita or trendy over-the-top jalapeño mezcal bs.) In the restaurant, service was attentive and smart. My burger was cooked perfectly and fries weren't soggy, plus there were only like 10 so I didn't feel like an enormous cow rolling out of there. Overall good times.

The Clocktower is a classy place. A little too expensive for my taste. If I spend hundreds on food then I expect it to be perfect, and then some. And it's really not here. The only thing that was standout was thier homemade ice cream. They had a bunch of different flavors from orange blossom to chai, hazelnut and vanilla. They also had sorbet. The orange blossom was my favorite flavor, its very delicate and light and has a nice floral note at the end reminiscent of rose water. It's a perfect cleanser and end to a meal. 

Service was very friendly and polite (got more friendly when we started ordering more than just one entree and a couple of drinks). The atmoshpere was cozy and classy. 

They give complementary bread which is bonus points (that is delicious). I love a place that does that. 

We split the strip steak. Its enough to feed two I thought, even though the waiter was definitely not happy we didn't each order an entree. The steak was great and the side of cauliflower was great too. The side was just so small though. 

Then we got the earl grey souffle, the honey cake and ice cream. The honey cake was dry. The earl grey suffle was okay, it did have a strong earl grey flavor. The ice cream was great!

The only reason I'm rating it 3 stars, and its a big one for me, is that I feel I can get the same food, just as good or better and more of it somewhere else. But I guess its expensive because its an iconic place and in a hotel. No matter what hotel restaraunts are always so expensive. Go here on a business dinner! Or if you have a gift card, like we did :)

I had been waiting for a long time to dine at The Clocktower; unfortunately, the experience was a disappointment. My fellow diner and I took four different dishes, two very good, two below par. The beef tartare was excellent, juicy, with an excellent and unusual dressing; the scallop too was delicious, served with lentils, cheddar and a duck coulis. The main dishes were disappointing. The preparation of the Dover Sole was sweetish, banal; the dish was very small and definitely not worth $50; the breast duck, on the other hand was huge, served as one big slab, with a coulis that was too citrusy and a minuscule "confit leg tarte". No proper accompaniment, partly our fault for not noticing the side dishes on the menu, but this was not brought to our attention by the waitress, as she should have done. Actually, the whole service was unsatisfactory. We waited forever for bread; when it appeared, it was piping hot, impossible to touch for five minutes with burning one's fingers. The sommelier appeared before we ordered our food: how could we choose a wine when we didn't yet know what we were going to eat?  Are patrons expected to pair the food with the wine rather than the other way round...? This said, the wine list was quite extensive. During the service, no waiter bothered to top up our glasses. Yes, the decor was attractive, but that is not enough to make for an enjoyable dining experience. One last, small but revealing thing: there were two metal coatracks next to the hostess's desk, where a proper closet would have been more appropriate for an allegedly four-star restaurant. We will not be back.

My fiance and I are from the philly area and are big Stephen Starr fans so while we were visiting NYC we wanted to try one of his restaurants and had heard good things about the clocktower. We were not disappointed.

We made reservations on the later side on a Saturday night so it wasn't overly crowded or loud- it was actually quite quiet considering the beautiful high ceilings in the main dining room. The overall atmosphere was cozy and moody with soft light that reminded me of being in an old, grand library. The service was exceptional throughout the meal. My fiance and I both tried a cocktail to start and then I switched to a glass of wine with dinner. All the beverages were great.

We started with the scallops and the beef tartare. Both appetizers were delicious but the scallops were especially tasty and cooked perfectly. For dinner we decided to share the 40 day dry aged prime rib which was also delicious plus the sides were amazing too, especially the foie gras salad. my fiance, who likes potatoes more than me, thought the potato gratin was exceptional. For dessert we had the Banoffee tarte which was STELLAR. 

overall, we had a great meal here and would definitely return.
The atmosphere can be a little confusing or dead and quiet because its in the hotel but the food is fenomenal

Grossly overpriced. Charged me close to 20 dollars for a tiny glass of champagne - probably only 2/3 of a glass. A burger that I could've gotten anywhere. A TINY chocolate almond mouse for 16 dollars. ridiculous how much people think they can charge

Celebrated my fiance's birthday here. An upscale restaurant but with friendly service and delicious food. Prices are definitely steep but a good place to frequent for a social night out. You go up the secluded winding staircase at the back which is quite romantic, and upstairs there is a bar right next to the restaurant where you can wait. Can ask for a private spot when you reserve, and if you mention prior it's a birthday, receive a slice of cake with a candle with is sweet. Scallops were great (but for that price, they damn should be). Duck and steak were cooked nicely.
Food was excellent. We went for lunch and it could have used more ambience (very few people there), but the food makes up for it.

This is the restaurant in The Edition Hotel.  The first morning we ate here it was okay. The pancakes were really good.  Just our food was cold... like the butter wouldn't melt (at all) in the oatmeal.  That's pretty cold.  The next morning it went from cold to worse.  They poured our coffee and didn't come back for TWENTY minutes with the cream.  It was kind of cold at that point. Give me a break.  The waiter had such an attitude.  Like sorry I want SLIGHTLY warm coffee. Dare to dream!

Excellent food and wine.  Had the Mac n cheese and fois gras appetizers and the duck and pork chop.  Very unique preparations for everything.  It was an excellent special occasion meal with great service.
Really great ambiance and great food. Went there for Saint Valentin. Always too expensive during those special occasion but still very nice.

What an amazing restaurant week lunch!!! The complimentary bread was so tasty and as soon as I cut into it it let out a huge puff of steam. I dunno how they did that but it was super effective, I was impressed. 

The monkfish was really tasty, super moist with a nicely sour sauce that made me want to keep eating. But it was the beet salad that I'm still thinking about a week later. The goat cheese was almost a foam, so light and creamy that it was almost like a mouthful of cool air. I have no idea what all the little dots and different beets were but it all combined into something fantastic. The thing that blew my mind though were the candies walnuts on them. I hate nuts, and yet these were so perfectly toasted that I was hobbling them up even without the salad! It was seriously the best beet salad I've ever heard, not to mention seriously beautiful

The restaurant definitely looks and feels very upscale. I love the decor (the walls are covered with various different paintings). I went there for brunch so the choices were more limited.

Food: 
English Breakfast (scrambled eggs, pork, sausage, bacon, pudding, mushroom)
Skirt steak and chips (steak with fries and pink peppercorn sauce)

The scrambled eggs were amazing (probably were one of the best I've had in my life). The toast that came along with it was way too hard and dry. I felt like the portion size of the steak was way too small for it to be that expensive. I ordered it medium rare but instead, it was medium well. The fries tasted like regular fries so no complaints there. The "salad" was whole pieces of lettuce...but the dressing was very subtle and not overwhelming.
The service was mediocre, and it's actually not hard getting a reservation here.

I had an exceptional dinner here tonight. I made a reservation to celebrate a friend's birthday. The food and service were both on point. The restaurant had a birthday note prepared on our table before we came and also gave us a complimentary drink to start. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful the entire evening.

We ordered the Roasted Maine Scallops to share. The scallops were perfectly cooked and the broth was quite delicious. I ordered the duck and my friend ordered the pork chop, both which we enjoyed thoroughly. For dessert, we ordered the Earl Grey soufflé with cognac cream. It was very flavorful and fluffy. The only warning is the soufflé does take a little bit to come out (I thought it was worth the wait).

I would definitely recommend The Clocktower. The experience was wonderful.
Sexy spot for post work drinks.  Intimate and exclusive with the bubbliest of proseccos.

One of the most cozy restaurants in New York. The food is excellent. Thee homemade bread and butter kicked off an outstanding meal. The sea urchin on daikon was perfectly executed. We had two excellent fish dishes, the halibut with sunchokes was possibly the best winter fish dish we have had. 

The great food, atmosphere and service will not leave you disappointed.

I went here for lunch during restaurant week with a few friends. The restaurant is beautiful! Presentation of the food was amazing. I got marinated yellowtail for appetizer which was good and for entree I chose the mushroom risotto. I was very disappointed because it was soooo salty that I couldn't finish my plate. I was not the only person who felt that way. My other 2 friends who ordered it as well felt the same way as well.

Food was delicious... many intricate and varying flavors. The dishes were artfully presented and felt very contemporary. The staff was nice. My one complaint is going to be the service... it was a bit on the slow side and not quite up to the level of other Michelin star restaurant I have visited. Regardless, I would recommend. eating at this restaurant.
Omg it was incredible.....  a bit pricy by well worth it.  I had the fillet with carrots omg... it is a must go.

Love love love the interior, it's like a secret place where you can have a date. Very friendly server, great service, amazing food and presentation. I loved every bite. They even give you complimentary dessert, it was so lovely and tasty.

I can understand the Michelin Star. To start I had the lobster with mussel mayo. The mayo was amazing, lobster presentation was great. For the second I had the burrata, which is lovable anywhere. Served cold with lemon confit. Very conserved presentation. For third I had the ox ckeek mac and cheese. All time favorite. Very fulfilling though so I dont reccomend if you expect to eat more. For the fourth i had the duck along with the Dover sole. You could smell the jus as it hit the duck. Lovely. The sole was phenomenal. Everything on that plate married together exquisitely. I would definitely recommend. Purple velvet pool table? Hell yeah!! Perfect for photos of a beautiful date. Overall great experience.

I love this restaurant.  It was a last minute decision to make a reservation; I am glad I did. The hostess, who was lovely, sat us next to the fireplace and we could see the whole room.  The lunch was fabulous. We ordered the macaroni and cheese with the mushrooms and beef tips.  It's not your typical macaroni with cheddar, but with several white cheeses. It was very tasty and filling. Great idea to add the beef & mushrooms because it adds richness to the plate.  We then had the chicken which is breast white meat. That came with a chicken leg confit topped with a small amount of greens, and on the plate were Brussels that were artfully presented which looked like a flower. The Brussels were the best I have tasted, ever! The chicken was moist and delicious, but the little dish of leg  confit, I could have eaten on my own.  Gil was our waiter and he was very on point and had a very charming personality.  He helped us with our order, thank goodness. There were so many dishes I wanted I couldn't make up my mind. I am sorry I didn't order the fish & chips, but that makes me just have to return. The decor was a setting out of an English country manor library. It's right off the park and one couldn't have a better place to dine.

Was pleasantly surprised by the food here. To start, the bread was amazing. I was then blown away by the ox cheek Mac and cheese, and the burger was top notch. Only thing that wasn't too special were the fries. Apple tart tartin for dessert was huge and delicious. Finally, complimentary jellies at the end of the meal were a nice touch.
Venison + steak + Mac cheese are all top notch. Wine list super long with great options. The place is fun and classy would for sure go back. Service also very good.
Had an afterwork dinner here on a Monday. Service was real good and the meals were just as great. Mac and cheese, Tartare and Mignon was amazing.

Main reason my wife and I wanted to check out The Clocktower is because after spending a few years in Philly, we became fans of the service level at Stephen Starr restaurants. Then we moved to California and there was no Stephen Starr to be found. Well, moving back east, we finally had the chance again, but in a new city! We chose The Clocktower first since it seemed to have the best reviews and the chef previously worked for Gordon Ramsay (my wife grew up in the UK so this is normal a selling point). The service definitely did not disappoint, and the food was amazing!

For a starter, I had the Foie Gras And Chicken Liver Parfait (see photo)... it was delicious. For dinner, the venison... also delicious. All the food was amazing. The service did not disappoint... one of the small things I really appreciated was the communication among the service team. For example, we told the hostess we were excited to try this place and were fans of Stephen Starr restaurants. At the END of the meal... an hour or so later... our server commented to us he heard we have been wanting to try the restaurant. I love little things like that - exactly the kind of hospitality I was hoping I would find.

We really enjoyed everything here.  Extensive wine list, great service, and creative twist on classic dishes with all the flavors there.  Michelin star worthy.  We also really enjoyed the ambience with a bright open room, high ceilings and framed pictures lining the walls.  They also have a room with a pool table with a bar nearby so will check that out next time. If you cant get into Eleven Madison that is nearby then you are not missing much by coming here.

Came here with coworkers for a super late bday celebration. Then filet mignon was perfection, medium rare and the home made fries amazing! Other dishes were the risotto, the monkfish, the halibut and the fish and chips. Loved the ambience and decor of the restaurant, super acquainted with the name of the restaurant simply fitting. Came here specifically for the soufflé this season was earl grey flavor, minus one star for the lateness of the soufflé even though I ordered it way ahead at the beginning of the meal. However they made it up and took the soufflé cost off as it took a full 40 mins before coming out as the first one apparently fell apart. The restrooms were super clean, service was good enough. Another restaurant off my bookmark

This restaurant really blew me away. I saw some negative reviews, which made me slightly hesitant but I personally had an amazing experience here.

The hostesses are so friendly, will check your coat for you. 
The restaurant is set up and it is a large space, each room is slightly separate from the others. 

Service is amazing. Wine list super extensive. Great cocktails. 

Food: 
Ox mac and cheese: Wow. Absolutely amazing. For an app, it's a pretty big portion. It's not the standard pasta they use in traditional mac n cheese, the cheese is absolutely amazing and the ox meat is sooo tender do not miss out on this! Our server acutally brought this out with our entree, as she recommended it would go better with that.

Apps: 
Foie gras with the duck prosciutto - comes with buttered white bread. The foie gras is absolutely decadent, you have to eat it with something to counter this crazy flavorful dish! Super good, and the thinly sliced prosciutto pieces are amazing as well.

Burrata - my friend argues it isn't burrata because the inside should be more creamy, and it was more on the solid side. Loved the sauce that accompanied it, it had a citrus flavor to it. 

Entree: 
Venison - so good. How often are you going to find this kind of meat at a restaurant? I would highly recommend taking advantage of it here. So delicious. You are given around 4/5 slices of this meat. Absolutely amazing. It also comes with vegetables. Quality over quantity, definitely.

Complimentary bread: Literally the best I have ever had at any restaurant. Homemade and the butter is delicious. 

Desserts: next time if I'm not about to hit a food coma, they have an apple tartin for 2. Otherwise, the other desserts are much smaller. We shared the mousse which was great. 

Their selection of teas is pretty fun, they're unique and all very high quality, many sourced from the UK. 

Great place, dark, intimate, great for all sorts of occasions. Oh and you also get a fairly nice view of Madison Square Park. I'd def come back!

This place is over priced and bad (this is the second time I've been and had the same experience both times) The service is so slow. The food is way too salty. The medium rare burger was well (they brought a new one). Chicken was pretty bad, very fatty. The burger was good but not better than a $15. Steak tartare was ok. Burrata was only ehh. The steaks were too salty. The fish was average. 


The only saving grace is the bread (though we had to ask 5 times to get it) and the Mac and cheese.

With these prices the food should be fantastic. It's only ok

This was hands down the most disappointing meal I've ever had and unfortunately it was on Thanksgiving. I went with two other friends, two of us got turkey and one got fish.

The turkey was severely undercooked and the sides the three of us were supposed to share were barely enough for one. I actually reported the turkey was undercooked to the staff and they said it was supposed to be that way. I was shocked by their response. (My friend threw up after she got home and i had an allergic reaction but the friend who got fish was fine.) The cornbread stuffing was literally just croutons, the mushrooms were severely dried out and the vegetables were pickled....who wants raw vegetables on thanksgiving? Anyone? No one. Also, nothing on our table was hot, not even warm.

When the staff cleared our plates, two of them barely had dents in them, and no one asked if there was anything wrong w our meal. Again, surprising for such a high end restaurant. Needless to say, don't waste your time or your money.

I came here with my husband and a friend for brunch. The place is great; the decor is English pub inspired, the food is good and well plated, the staff is friendly and attentive. I would highly recommend this if you are looking for an upscale vibe, good food, and an unpretentious place. I will reiterate that the decor and ambiance is well done.

The service was terrible and the food was okay. This was a big disappointment and I was expecting so much more. Since the minute we were seated, it seemed the waiter didn't want us there. He didn't give me a menu, but gave one to my male partner which was odd. It could be a slip of the mind but for the prices and what the restaurant is trying to present, it didn't seem acceptable. We finished our appetizers and he gave us the dessert menu before we received our main dish ( which was the duck for two). Again like he wanted us to leave. At that point the manager or someone got involved. When the duck was finally served, it was completely cold. We returned the food and left. I can't believe we had to pay for this meal thankfully they didn't put the cold duck on the bill. It was a terrible experience. For the prices and vibe they are trying to pull off The staff should care about their patrons. The shake shack outside in the park would have been better service and hot food.

Great food, atmosphere, n service. For food that I found outstanding: the scallop in broth (app), pork chops (main), venison dish (main). Sadly the pigeon dish was not available at that time. A lot of stairs to get to the restaurant lol.

Not the most memorable of experiences.  Cool atmosphere.  Great drinks.  Food was just alright.  Beef tartare was the best thing I had all night.  Duck entree was solid.  Girlfriend ordered the filet and ended up sending it back.  Second one was definitely much better, but still pretty mediocre.

Clocktower is nestled in a cosy space above the lobby of the EDITION hotel across from Madison Square Park. Being a collaboration between the famed restaurateur Stephen Starr and British Chef Jason Atherton (enjoyed his Michelin starred Pollen Street Social in London) -- it's no ordinary hotel dining room. Given the talent backing The Clocktower, as well as its Michelin star, it seemed like a solid choice. Overall, though, while we found the menu to be well conceived, the dishes need more editing and finesse. Would love to give 4 stars to the very personable staff and cozy environment, but the food fell short of expectations at this level and our wine selection was served at an improper temperature, so rounding down to 3 stars.

Atmosphere
- Clubby enclave that really suits the concept, not staid/stuffy though.
- Warm and inviting with several distinct rooms, dimmed lighting and classic British design elements.
- Tables are nicely spaced for NYC.

Food
Everything sounds great in concept, and to be sure the flavor profiles were all nice. Some dishes felt like they were missing components, while others could use a touch more refinement. Menu descriptions are elaborate and try overly hard to connote farm-to-table. The anticipation generated is fulfilled unevenly. Entrees were lackluster, while apps and desserts hit high notes. We had:

-Hudson Valley Foie Gras And Chicken Liver Parfait (london stout, lentils, smoked duck - $19): Highlight dish - foie with lentils and stout very innovative pairings. Well done!
-Long Island Tomatoes (sauternes and tomato gelée, shaved brooklyn burrata, olive biscuit, peppermint - $20): Tasty, but unexceptional, despite the enticing description.
- Long Island Duck Breast (spiced peppercorn, grilled peach with Argan, pickled kohlrabi, five plum sauce - $ 39): Cooked to good temp, but wish fat was a bit further rendered. Served as one large piece of meat, without any accompaniment to add balance and interest.
- Berkshire Pork Chop (beetroot soubise, white balsamic puffs, semi-dried chioggia beets, black pudding, charcuterie sauce - $37): Moist, with the white balsamic puffs lending a nice textural element. Favorite of our proteins.
- Strawberries and Cream (vanilla custard, olive oil cake, red verjus sorbet -  $15): Loved it! Top caliber with nice nuance and great interplay of textures; sweet but not overwhelming.

Beverage
Having had cocktails downstairs at The Lobby Bar (nice environment), went straight for wine. Upon seating, you will be presented a "Champagne cart" which seemed cool in concept (some may find it hokey). In general, wine list had good breath across regions and solid options in various price points, including sub $150. 

Somm suggested the 2013 Odoul-Coquard Aux Saint Jacques ($152), a very solid Nuits-Saint-Georges Burgundy - good recommendation. Sadly, it was served very close to room temperature, which is unexpected for this caliber of venue. Should we have made a comment? Probably, but hated to see a nice bottle go to waste and everyone was just too nice. It didn't kill the experience, but was disappointing.

Service
- Waitress very personable and attentive, delivered great service.
- Somm did good job interacting, happy to discuss the wine list and perceptive to our tastes and budget. Really nice job, except should have detected wine temp before serving.

From the moment we sat the service was so friendly and attentive. Complimentary champagne and a handwritten note was given with seemingly every special event. Great way to start our anniversary dinner. Every bite of food we had was amazing. We had the chilled Boston lobster, steak tartare and fois gras for our appetizers and all were absolutely delicious. For dinner the duck and pork chop, typically I don't have a pork chop as my number one pick on a menu, but it was so tender and flavorful. For dessert we had the ice cream and sorbet selection. We were congratulated on our anniversary by the lovely gm David. I would absolutely visit again so experience more of what The Clocktower has to offer.

Came for brunch. The service needs some work. I thought the food was good. They forgot the tea cup with the tea, and didn't come back to the table until they were clearing. Also, gave us two different menus to start, not a big deal just needs a bit of work for a one star restaurant.

Best experience ever. This is my second time dining at Clocktower's. Services was great professional and friendly. Food was delicious. I definitely come 
Back again

Had dinner here with some friends.  The food and service were excellent!! Just look at the photos...!!  Of course the best was the pistachio soufflé with a dab of chocolate ice cream....hmm hmm, yum yum!!

Great food, service and old school ambience, that deserve a 5 star.  Yes highly recommend it!!

Maybe I had very high expectations from last time, but didn't think this time things were as good. The two appetizers we got had gelatin in it, which I get it, it is great to offer something different and mix different flavors, but I thought it was over used.
We got (2 people):
- Scottish Langoustine Tartare ($22): grapefruit gelée, avocado, finger lime, anise leaves. A shrimp tartare, without the egg yok and little grapefruit jello mixed in. Loved the taste, hated the texture. Made it seem like caviar from a far, but it wasn't 
- Marinated Yellowtail ($21): seaweed custard, bonito gelée, spring onion and ginger salad. Square pieces of marinated yellow tail on a base of - again - jello like base. This put me off.
- Braised Atlantic Halibut ($44): salt baked baby carrots, dulse seaweed, yuzu, lobster, pink grapefruit. Really good tasty fish. The baby carrots abnd the grapefruit had a mild sweet taste that went very well with the fish. Lobster is just  a tiny bit, don't expect too much.
- Long Island Duck Breast ($39): spiced peppercorn, grilled peach with Argan, pickled kohlrabi, five plum sauce. My bf licked, I tried it and liked the plum sauce it came with.
I will wait a few months to come back again, so they change the menu a bit and I can try things without gelatin.
Duck dinner is really good, as well as apple pie dessert. Atmosphere is cool- but tables are on top of each other.

A Marriott dining room by any other Name is a Marriott dining room
A discrete entrance on Madison, a sweeping circular staircase or a high tech elevator to this reimagined Met Life office space with lots of paneling, molding, an old fashion billard room cum bar,  flaming gas fireplaces raising the temperatures on a sticky August afternoon, wooden benches in the lobby for waiting and waiting and waiting--20 minutes for a 1:00p.m. reservation--our table was being "dressed"  and a congenial wait staff, some of whom seem to be waiters, others who may be captains, bus people, and then an undefined group of floaters in street clothes--those descended later when after an hour our entrees arrived and we were given the wrong entree.  We ordered oxtail pie, we were given a kind of fish stew.  It took a while to get someone's attention, and when we did get a bus person--the waiter seemed to have disappeared--one of the un-uniformed floaters appeared, apologized, sent for another, they conferred, promised the pie and left the fish,now chilling and floating in an unappealing glaze in case we wanted to eat it.  Nobody seemed to want to remove it from the table, although they finally took the silverware.  It took another 20 minutes for the right entree to arrive. And another 5 to present a clean knife and fork on a wooden tray. My friend had, of course, finished her chicken breast, the dining room was practically empty and it was 3:00 p.m.  And our captain who had been initially friendly, now realizing we were probably not going to be generous tippers was remarkably officious, plunking the bill down with a curt, "Whenever you're ready."  Granted it is restaurant week, not a time when restaurant food is at its best, but that's not an excuse for an inept wait-staff and an inattentive kitchen.  The food, certainly hotel-dining room quality-- even though that ox was ground up mystery meat  and the foie gras parfait served on a bed of lentils, was a peculiar melange, probably is adequate for the tourists paying top dollar to stay in a luxury Marriott and the regular menu prices are high enough to have that bespoken quality and the ghosts of all those MetLife employees who brown-bagged it for lunch are floating though these rooms wondering why people are paying so much to eat in an office.
Food was nothing spectacular.  The monkfish was bland.  Service was the real disappointment.  Very very slow.
The service and food are always top notch. The Hostess Tanya is amazing and is always accommodating and friendly. Definitely a great place to bring clients and friends.

I came on a Sunday, but was surprised that the place isn't more buzzing - the food totally justifies many more customers! Guess it's a hidden gem, since it's hard to know from the outside where the restaurant really is.

This is my second time visiting (came here over a year ago), and enjoyed it just as much. It's a very unique concept done by two starr (pun intended) restaurateurs, and you can definitely feel the "UK-ness" of the place with the framed pictures of celebrities and the city covering the walls and the dark stained wood decor. The lobby is really something with the billiards table and bar while you wait for your friends or table. Food wise, we got the foie gras, sea urchin, duck breast, halibut, and chocolate dessert. The bread was quite nice, crusty on the outside and hot and fluffy on the inside. It was a really rich dinner, but I finished every bite, and was particularly impressed with quality of the halibut (a fish that can easily be overcooked and dry). Standards have not dropped with age, evidently.

Good food. But awful service. 
We have to hunt for our server all night long. And the server has zero idea about wine. She gave us wrong information, poured wrong beverage all the time. And pushed all responsibilities to the sommelier, who was also someone we have to hunt for. 
This sounds funny but the tables are tiny, and can hardly fit our food. Because the chef loves to use gigantic presentation plate! So during the dinner, we spent a lot of time moving our plates around and try to be comfortable. And the server/busser didn't attempt to help at all. They just put everything on the table and leave us struggling on our own. 
Such a waste on the good food. 
Also, the manager was extremely arrogant, when we complained about the the service. He argued with us and act like he's smarter than his customers. If he kindly accepted our comments, everything will be fine. But he has such ego problem. 
What kind of Michelin star restaurant is this? Please spend your money and time elsewhere.

We came in for lunch for restaurant week that runs about $26 for a two course menu. Our server was great and the food was also very good. The bread they serve looks good, but was really tough. The butter was delicious but breaking through the tough, rubbery exterior of the bread made it tough to eat. Looking around, most people didn't even touch it. 

The foie gras parfait was nicely plated and came with a side of bread. The lentils added a nice texture to the creamy liver dish. It was also sort of sweet and nutty, with small prices or duck sprinkled around. 

The risotto with lobster reduction was very good but could have been a little warmer.

The ox cheek and ale pie was delicious. It came with an oyster sauce they pour tableside and had a delicious dark sauce that encircles the pie. The crust was perfect, but again, I thought the food could have been warmer. 

The flavors were great, service was spectacular, but the timing at which the food came out could have been better. We saw them bring our entrees out right after our first courses made their way to the table so they turned around and brought it back in, which is probably why the food was more on the lukewarm side. Maybe a little miscommunication on the part of timing. But don't let that stop you from paying them a visit. The restaurant is up a set of spiral stairs. They've also got a cool bar to sit and grab a cocktail while you wait.

Food was pretty good. It was not super memorable though. Honestly the one thing I remembered was the bread. Everything was good but just not outstanding. I really like the restaurant decoration and the vibe. It is a classy, high end place. Service was great. Waiters fold your napkins when you leave your seat. Overall I enjoyed the visit here.

The service is wonderful and the food is delightful. I The champagne risotto was my favorite - definitely recommend. We also had the ox cheek which was super filling. It came out like a shepherds pie. Also enjoyed the monkfish, the sauce is very tasty but the chunks of monkfish in the sauce were not the best for me. I would have preferred the whole fish to come out but I get it might not have looked as nice. What a nice place overall!

Love the food and the staff here. Since you walk in the bar, everyone is smiling. Super nice. Honestly there's a lot of restaurants making good food in NYC, but not all of them can provide a good service. Plus there's a very unique dining area. They deserve the Michelin reward.

Today I had a lovely experience at The Clocktower.  There were 4 of us and we had the Restaurant Week menu. 
The food was delicious and beautifully presented.
The service was impeccable.  Thank you Marta and Lise.
Food is too salty and too much fat in it.  This caused me stomach upset for the rest of day.

Breakfast service at the restaurant was not what we expected. Our waitress was extremely inefficient and rude and did not write down our order so naturally all of it came out wrong. When we asked her for the side of potatoes we ordered, she had an attitude about it and we ended up getting it after we ate our meal. I had specified my allergies and told her that I could not have banana but she failed to write that down so naturally she brought me granola with giant slices of banana. 

We had to constantly ask for our plates to be taken up, get refills or flag down another tables waitress to eat our order right. 

Since we were staying at the hotel attached to the restaurant, she didn't give us our check at the end and said it will be billed to the room. To our surprise, the check had items we didn't even order and the charge was much higher than what we calculated. Overall, the waitress left us with a  sour taste in our mouth. 

As far as food, there are no gluten free or vegan options other than avocado toast. They don't even have gluten free bread. I had to order oats with berries which was $20. 

If you are staying at the hotel, head somewhere else for breakfast and try them for dinner or lunch when the head chef is there.

Gorgeous Space with excellent food and great service.     The decor and actual physical space is one of the nicest in NYC.    Very high ceilings and beautiful array of photos and comfortable seating make for fine dining.       The Chicken for 2 at $90 was very tasty as was the scallops app. - small but very good.     Service was very attentive and friendly.

This rating is only for the small and very intimate bar. We tasted one of the barman's composition (cucumber, tequila and some other flavors) multiple times and enjoyed more at each glass.  Will come back to eat here

Only came for cocktails and enjoyed this old school high end cocktail bar. Jason Athertons desire to make a brutish cocktail bar was executed perfectly. Wood paneling, black and white photos in mismatching frames, and a pool table help bring this place to life. I only had two rounds of cocktails on a Wednesday evening but the place was alive and the cocktails were top notch. I hunt down great cocktails and this place delivered and will be a spot I bring colleagues and friends for evening drinks. Will try the restaurant soon enough as I was able to dine at Jason's spot in Cebu, Philippines and the food was excellent.
For the price average! Was good but for that price I would expect a little more! Although excellent service and lovely experience!!

Recently revisited for a date night, and had a much better experience this time around. I made a reservation online easily for 7:30 a few weeks in advance, but the restaurant didn't have many empty tables while we were there so I'd definitely plan ahead.

Started off the night with the Royal Engagement and The Don for drinks, both of which were very sippable. The Don came with a side of chocolate candies to enjoy with the drink as well.

As many other reviewers have noted, the complimentary bread and butter is amazing. You get an entire mini loaf of fresh baked bread (seriously, when we cracked it open it was still steaming) and salted, whipped butter. 

For food, we split a half dozen oysters, ox cheek mac and cheese, and the baked chicken for two. Everything was delicious (especially that mac and cheese). The chicken was prepared 3 ways - the white meat came plated with morels and some sort of puree, while the dark meat came in mini sliders and a separate pot with jus poured over it. So good! Not as good as the Nomad chicken, but still delicious.

Dessert was the apple tarte tatin for two (the panna cotta from last time is no longer on the menu, thankfully), which was seriously one of the best desserts I've had. Nothing fancy about it, just a perfectly prepared apple tart with caramel sauce drizzled all over it, and I couldn't ask for more.

Meal ended with complimentary almond financiers. 

Would definitely come back here for another special (or even not so special) occasion. 

Also - they have the best smelling hand soap I've ever used.

This restaurant is very nice with delicious food and impeccable service.
I had the mousse de fois gras wich is an interesting twist on one of my favorite dish then we shared a dry age cote de boeuf both were awesome.
Highly recommended.

Had dinner here last weekend for F's birthday. I like the ambiance in here; dim and romantic. The high ceilings and the wall to wall gold framed images make quite a statement. 

We were told by the hostess that we only had until 9:15 until they had another party booked for the table. It's always annoying to hear this; I'm sure it's a necessary practice so that they can seat as many parties as possible in a night, but please keep that practice behind closed doors. In the end, there were plenty of tables open and we weren't asked to leave... but in the back of our minds, it was lingering there and we opted not to order extra drinks after we finished our bottle of wine. 

They started us off with a small glass of sparkling wine because they knew we were there to celebrate a birthday, which was very nice. 

We ordered the $125 seafood platter to start. It read like it would be huge and at that price point we thought it would be so we didn't order any additional appetizers... but it turned out to be very small. I'm sure I could've easily finished the whole platter myself. 

I ordered the pork chop. It was well cooked, but there was lots of fat - and in the dimness of the restaurant, you couldn't always see if it was meat or fat. I don't eat the fat on meats so whenever I got a bite of fat, I had to suppress the urge to spit it out (fancy place as it is). But others who love fat might like this; A joked that it sounds delicious. 

Friends ordered the duck, lamb and burger and all seemed to enjoy their dishes. 

F got the pistachio soufflé. This takes 20 minutes to make but it's worth the wait. It was light, fluffy and delicious. A and I shared the warm mango pudding. Texturally, I thought it was kinda weird and flavor wise, there was nothing special about it. F and J tried a bite each, but no one on the table liked the dish much. Most of it was left. 

The service isn't very warm or affable. It started out very friendly when we got the sparkling wine and waters... but we waited a while before a waiter came to take our order and even then, he only came by after we waved him over. (We had been told we had to leave by a certain time, so we wanted to make sure we can place our appetizer order early so we would have timers leisurely enjoy our entrées.) When he came by, he told us he would prefer if we ordered everything all together instead of just the appetizer cuz it would make things easier. Ok. Luckily, by the time he arrived to our table, we all knew what we wanted so it was fine. 

Overall, we had a solid 3 star experience. The chef has a Michelin star restaurant in the UK, so I am glad we tried it, but I don't think I will be looking to dine there if I'm ever visiting the country based on this dining experience.

Went with friends for a birthday dinner. To start, staff is off. We were the first to arrive for a party of 4. We checked in and were just standing there, the host didn't offer for us to wait at the bar, take our coats, offer a drink or to be seated while we await our friends. We walked downstairs on our own to wait at the lounge. After we were seated for dinner, the waiter asked what kind of water we wanted. I think he asked but never listened. They poured everyone the same Perrier water, after 2 of us asked for still water. Then they screwed up the entrees by bringing the wrong meal
To the wrong person. Food was just ok for the price they charge. Service is poor at best. Eleven Madison Park is up the block- go there for a better experience

Ok, so we came for the Dover Sole... which they ran out of after we ordered.  Mildly disappointed would be a kind way to put it.  A birthday dinner long planned, but it's not something that could have been helped, I guess.

Drinks were nice, the food well crafted (though I'm not sure I'd go back to the filet... I mean, we'll obviously be getting the Dover sole).  The decor is beautiful and the approach sequence coming up the spiral stairs is wonderful.  Staff from the hostess to the wait staff was fantastic and helped us get over the disappointment as much as they could.

Note: if you want the sole make sure to let them know in advance!

AMAZING SERVICE. DELICIOUS. COME HERE. 5 STARS.
-
I reserved this place for our corporate holiday dinner for 9 people. We were seated in the main dining hall. You can book the billiards room and lounge. It's NYC, you can do anything at the right price.

For the first time ever, I recommend everything ordered:
Starters: 
- Complimentary bread & butter: Best bread.
- East and west coast oysters ($37) for a dozen: Excellent
- Berners Tavern mac and cheese ($26): Decadent, slightly too rich for me but perfectly cooked and tender.
- Marinated yellowtail ($21): Small portion, still delicious
- Roasted Maine scallops ($23): Cauliflower was an excellent addition. Scallops were divine. 
- Dry aged Creekstone beef tartare ($21): Get this if you love tartare.

Entrees:
Long Island duck breast ($39): Perfectly cooked med rare.
Rack of Colorado lamb ($45): Perfectly cooked med rare. Lancashire hotpot comes in this little pan, and was too rich for me and even the peppermint relish couldn't cut it. But the few bites I had were incredible. 

Drinks:
- Social Soda ($9), P's & Q's: Delicious
- Social Soda ($9), Orange Whip: Slightly too sweet for me
I don't drink alcohol, but most of the cocktails were excellent according to my team. About $16 per cocktail.

Dessert:
- Tartin for two ($25): Incredible, that ice cream was good too!
- Warm mango pudding ($15): Divine. Felt that the mango was kind of stringy, but still delicious
- Goat cheese parfait ($15): Unexpected dark horse, that beet tuile smashed expectations. Recommend this over the tartin if you're seeking a savory dessert rather than sweet.

Visited this restaurant for lunch during restaurant week in February with some co-workers and it was by far my favorite of all the places we tried that week. I had the cornish fish stew and if I could have licked the plate I would have. For my main I had the Atlantic cod and I realized I have been eating over cooked fish all my life. Lastly, for desert we shared the panna cotta and a sweet potato pie mini thing that was the best. I really can't say enough how much I loved this place and want to make dinner plans with my husband so he can experience it as well.

Visited this past Saturday, reservation was for 8:15 and the restaurant was packed.  Decor was very gentlemen library - looks like a place where the boys would enjoy a scotch and cigar.  The restaurant is split into 5 rooms - 3 for dining, 1 is the bar, and another houses a pool table (nice touch).

Complimentary sourdough bread arrived fresh from the oven, good crust and soft flesh.  Seafood tower to start for our group of 4, and this is what you get for $125:  4 oysters, 2 lobster claws, 4 crab claws (very small for "king crab") 4 Maya shrimps, and a sauce dish size of each of the oscietra caviar (1/2 tsp of caviar on creme fresh), scallop crudo, shrimp salad, and crab trifle.  All the seafood were cooked expertly, and the raw items were fresh.

For mains we tried 2xhalibut and 2xduck breast.  My DCs enjoyed the halibut but it was disappointing to me (I order fish fairly frequently).  There was nothing wrong with it, but nothing special either, other than the chestnut gnocchi (2 pieces), which was divine.  Would've rather had a plate of it as my main.  The duck breast was the better of the two IMO, bold flavours that complimented each other, breasts succulent and confit crispy.

Pistachio souffle for dessert, which was well executed.  Rich, eggy, delicious, although slightly lacking in pistachio flavour.  Complimentary raspberry petite fours were tasty.

Service, for the type of restaurant, was bad.  Sommelier whispered something to our DC who did the picking but provided zero info to the rest of the table - and 3 of us were sharing.  We were seated for a good 20 min before our waiter even came by to say hi.  No intros to mains (we did get an intro with the seafood tower) during delivery and no follow-up after delivery.  Was another 15 min after our mains were cleared that we were asked about dessert.  Not once were we asked if we wanted more beverages until dessert, even though a couple of our glasses sat empty.  The restaurant appeared well staffed so not sure what this was about.  Server was polite when we managed to have him around.

Overall, good enough that I don't regret going, but no reason to return.

Came here for an anniversary dinner with my husband. Loved the ambiance, very different, did not feel like your typical New York restaurant which I appreciated. They welcomed us with a card wishing us happy anniversary as well as a toast. 

We started with the macaroni and cheese appetizer, typically served with ox cheek, but we asked for it vegetarian. It had this really delicious saltiness to it that I liked, could have been warmer but overall very good. 

I had the creekstone skirt steak medium rare, which was a little fatty, but flavorful and well cooked. My husband ordered the filet mignon, which was extremely tender and delicious. Both of our steaks came with frites, but we opted to substitute one of the sides for the potato gratin-- I cannot recommend this enough! Creamy and garlicky, the gratin was my favorite part of the meal.

The only reason The Clocktower gets four stars instead of five is the dessert- the apple tarte tartine for two was underwhelming. Served with caramel sauce and vanilla ice cream on the side, it was not warm enough, and the tarte itself was somehow too sweet with average crust. 

Definitely check this place out, just skip the dessert!

My colleague and I went for a weekday dinner without reservation. In the order of events:
Doorman and check in staff: Professional, polite and lovely!
Ambience: 5 stars. Love this place!
Wait staff: Professional, polite and attentive!
FOOD : Delicious!! Being a vegetarian, I was pleased to be offered an exclusive menu which is now becoming a trend at lots of places. Finally us plant eaters are being respected for our choices than being an after thought on the menu. I ordered  the chestnut gnocchi with hen of the wood mushroom and pureed lentils and 3 days later I am still thinking about it. Oh! The warm home made bread loaf took us to food heaven. My colleague ordered a burger and loved it too!
Bill: reasonable for the quality of food. 

Lastly, why 4 stars? Dirty restroom

Will I return and recommend? Most definitely! 

Sorry no pictures as my motto for this year is to enjoy the moment than click through them!

Blech, I was expecting a lot more than the food we received at this Michelin-starred restaurant...although a lot of the 1 Michelin-starred restaurants in NYC seem to be overrated these days.  The tart marinade of the yellowtail completely overpowered the fish, and the meats we ordered, the duck and the bone-in NY strip, both came out so dry.  Overall, was very underwhelmed with the experience and would not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

Perfect place to take your parents out for lunch.

Fancy restaurant serving modernized timeless english food. Decor is attractive and food quality meets the expectations. 

Its location in flatiron makes it more accessible and that much more attractive as well - definitely will be back
A very nice bar with excellent drinks.  Great ambiance.  A wonderful hidden gem in the neighborhood.

Located in a nice hotel right next to Madison Square Park, the inner decoration is classic. Whole restaurant is separated into multiple spacious dining room. The dining area we were sitting is not loud at all. It's a good place for business occasion.
I really enjoy the warm served sourdough before dishes. 
Overall: great service, great environment, starters much better than entree. 
The starter was absolutely amazing. We ordered the smoked salmon and English cucumber soup. Very nice display and taste. 

For entree we ordered strip steak and duck breast. The strip steak was amazing! But the grocery store style salad came with it was very disappointing for the price of the dish...
A bit disappointed with the duck entree too.. Duck meat was too dry. Also I could feel somewhere the window was open, so my dish was getting cold quick.

We came here for a quick drink before we went to get dinner. This place is really cute and a great place to go with friends for a drink or on a date. There's a pool table there for entertainment! We each had one drink. It was really good, not too sweet and not too strong, but the drink was really expensive!

Nice menu at the Clocktower however service was poor this evening. There is also a lack of professionalism in the Kitchen the steaks were both seriously under cooked.  All of our dishes lacked seasoning a bit of salt and pepper would have helped a lot.   I do give credit to the floor manager for trying to help the poor servers and making up for the kitchens mistakes.  It's worth another try perhaps they'll fix the issues.io

The main course, pork and chicken is really amazing, especially the pork.

The pork has crispy edge but really soft inner. Also the pumpkin and its sauce is really delicious. The chicken has bread pastry and really soft chicken and yummy mushroom.

Besides, the fish appetizers has yummy and soft fish. The bread is really crispy.

The dessert is not as good as Cafe Boulud but also really good. I like the soft white chocolate. How do the cook finish it?

This is a great place for either a nice business lunch or a date dinner.  Classy Hotel restaurant serving innovative designs on classic dishes.

The foie gras and the yellow tail starters are both beautiful, like works of art!

Came here with a friend on a Thursday night and was pleasantly surprised. It has an old school feel to it with the timeless photos. The service was amazing, the atmosphere has a classic NY feel, and the food was on point.
